description:
On February 21, 2008, the City entered into a Statement of Work with Sensus for the implementation of the advanced water metering infrastructure (AMI) system and later approved upgrades to the Sensus Analytics Enhanced Package, including cloud hosting and the Sensus Customer Portal. This AMI system provides accurate and timely meter data to support utility billing, customer service, water conservation initiatives, and long-term utility planning.
The Sensus Customer Portal is now being retired. On October 20, 2025, the City Commission approved Vertex One as the replacement customer portal. Because the existing portal is being phased out, a new agreement with Sensus is required to reflect the revised terms of service.
The updated Software as a Service (SaaS) agreement incorporates the City’s existing Sensus hosted software solution, leased spectrum, technical support, and all associated terms and conditions required for the continued operation of the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) platform. The agreement also adds language to facilitate the use of the Vertex Customer Portal component approved by the Commission on October 21, 2025, and removes the Sensus Customer Portal component being retired.
Sensus is the sole source manufacturer for the City’s water meters and AMI software services, and Core & Main is the sole source provider of Sensus products. In Fiscal Year 2025, the SaaS fee totals $30,385.38. This fee is a flat annual cost subject to a three percent (3%) annual escalation.
title: Approval of Sensus Software as a Service Agreement. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
In 2025, the City of Ocoee Utilities Department staff initiated a review of alternative pumps for its lift stations due to increased product lead times and rising costs for FLYGT pumps. During this evaluation, Shinmaywa pumps came highly recommended as cost-effective alternative for pumps up to 25 HP.
To verify Shinmaywa pumps performance and reliability, Utilities staff performed reference checks with Gainesville Regional Utilities (GRU) and Jacksonville Electrical Authority (JEA), two of the largest sewer providers in Florida that use these pumps. After a site visit with maintenance staff at JEA and a pilot study where lift station staff ran a Shinmaywa pump next to existing pumps in Ocoee lift stations, it was determined that Shinmaywa pumps are a suitable replacement for FLYGHT pumps up to 25 HP . In addition to pump performance, Shinmaywa pumps can be delivered in a more timely manner since they are stocked in Atlanta and Charlotte, and they represent a 30% savings per pump compared to FLYGT pumps. Additionally, the pumps do not require any modifications for installation.
Power and Pumps is the supplier of Shinmaywa pumps. The further use of Power and Pumps requires single source vendor approval as any additional purchases will exceed the purchasing authority of the City Manager’s office.
title: Approval of Power and Pumps as Single Source Vendor for Small Lift Station Pumping Repairs and Replacements. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
The Orange County criminal justice partners have developed a collaborative agreement to improve public safety and enhance offender supervision throughout the county. The agreement seeks approval for the Ocoee Police Department to formally participate in this partnership, designed to strengthen the administration of criminal justice and reentry services. Through improved communication, efficient information exchange, and coordinated problem-solving, the agreement focuses on reducing recidivism, enhancing offender accountability, and maximizing the use of shared resources. Each participating entity retains responsibility for its own personnel and administrative operations while committing to mutual goals that benefit the broader community.
Under the agreement, the Florida Department of Corrections will undertake several operational responsibilities to support the Ocoee Police Department in managing offenders within the City of Ocoee. These responsibilities include identifying high- and at-risk offenders, sharing timely information such as addresses, criminal histories, and supervision conditions, and conducting field administrative supervision duties. The Department will also provide warrants, perform warrantless arrest procedures when appropriate, and participate in ride-a-longs with Ocoee officers to ensure familiarity with the locations, behaviors, and supervision requirements of community control offenders, sexual offenders, sexual predators, and other high-risk individuals.
The agreement further outlines the duties requested of the Ocoee Police Department, pending City Commission approval. These responsibilities include assisting probation officers with field operations, warrant and warrantless arrests, surveillance of high-risk offenders, and ensuring safety during administrative searches. The Department is also asked to assist with transporting offenders, securing property seized during searches, and communicating violations observed by Ocoee officers. Both agencies agree to jointly pursue public-safety initiatives, coordinate reentry support services, share information, and avoid duplication of efforts. By approving this contract, the City Commission would authorize the Ocoee Police Department to participate in this partnership formally, ensuring continued collaboration that enhances community safety and strengthens offender reentry efforts throughout Orange County.
This agreement shall be in effect for a period of five (5) years, beginning on April 29, 2026, and ending on April 28, 2031.
title: Approval of a Memorandum of Agreement between the Florida Department of Corrections and Ocoee Police Department. (Police Chief Ogburn)

description:
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) has developed a regional, multi-jurisdictional Abduction Response Team (CART) to enhance the rapid and coordinated response to missing, endangered, or abducted children. The initiative brings together trained personnel, investigative resources, equipment, and expertise from multiple Central Florida law enforcement agencies. As outlined in the agreement, participating agencies agree to mutually support one another, exchange information, and provide specialized assistance when activated for CART operations.
CART participation strengthens operational readiness during high-risk incidents by establishing clear procedures for requesting aid, supervisory authority, and jurisdiction. FDLE has developed regional, multi-jurisdictional child boundaries, documentation requirements, evidence handling, and inter-agency coordination. The agreement also clarifies liability, cost responsibilities, complaint procedures, and obligations to partner agencies, ensuring a structured and accountable response model that aligns with FDLE statewide standards. Each agency remains responsible for the acts and omissions of its personnel while participating in CART activities. Agencies supply necessary personnel and resources without creating financial obligations for other partners.
The Ocoee Police Department has historically collaborated with regional and state partners in cases involving endangered children, and formal participation in CART will significantly enhance the Department’s ability to leverage critical resources during time-sensitive investigations. Approval of this agreement ensures that Ocoee officers can both request and provide specialized assistance during CART deployments, further enhancing public safety for the residents of Ocoee. This agreement will be in effect until December 31, 2028.
title: Approval of a Voluntary Cooperation Mutual Aid Agreement between the City of Ocoee, Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE), and other Participating Regional Agencies, to form an Orlando Regional Operations Center Child Abduction Team. (Police Chief Ogburn)

The tower base station collects and transmits meter data for water billing, and the existing tower antenna base station utilizes outdated technology and has reached the end of its useful life. Core & Main, who is the sole source provider of Sensus products, has provided a quote of $67,540.54 to install a new base station that is supported by a five-year protection plan.

description:
The 8” force main on North Clarke Road, north of A.D. Mims Road, has experienced several breaks and requires replacement to avoid future pipe breaks. The force main replacement has been split into two phases. Phase 1 was completed with the Clarke Road Widening project. Phase 2 runs approximately 550 feet north of Ocoee Vista Parkway and runs south to AD Mims Road and includes the relocation of the existing Florida Central Railroad (FCEN) crossing. Relocation of the railroad crossing removes the current point of connection from under pavement in the intersection of Wurst Road and Clarke Road into a grass area adjacent to Wurst Road.
To construct any utilities under the railroad tracks, the City must first enter into a licensing agreement with FCEN. Past agreements with FCEN have required the City to pay an annual license fee that increases each year based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI). To avoid recurring yearly fees with escalation, staff is requesting approval of a one-time application fee of $1,500.00 and a one-time license fee of $24,400.00. The existing annually reoccurring licensing agreement will be terminated upon completion of the force main relocation and the the one-time license fee will provide the City with substantial savings over the lifetime of the agreement.
title: Approval of License Agreement Between Florida Central Railroad Company, LLC (FCEN) for the Clarke Road Force Main Relocation Project. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
On November 18, 2025, the City Commission approved advertising a Resolution of Intent to Use the Uniform Method of Collection for Non-Ad Valorem Special Assessment. This resolution provides the Commission flexibility in determining payment options for the 41 downtown customers required to connect to the City sewer system under state law (Section 381.00655(1)(a), Florida Statutes) and the 2016 Bond, which funded much of the downtown sewer construction. The City has also secured a $700,000 Florida Springs Protection Grant to cover construction costs for connecting the 41 private properties. A condition of the grant is that all customers comply with state law and complete the sewer connection.
Although the grant reduces customer costs by more than 50%, it does not cover the sewer capital fee mandated by City Code and the 2016 Bond. To assist residents with this fee, the Utilities Department is evaluating payment options for Commission consideration. One option is a non-ad valorem tax assessment, which would allow participating customers to make installment payments through their tax bill.
To keep this payment option available for Commission consideration, resolution adoption must occur before January 1, 2026. Potential payment options to assist customers with the sewer connection will be brought to the Commission for consideration at a later date.

description:
On November 18, 2025, the City Commission approved assuming full operational ownership of Forest Lake Golf Club and directed the City Manager to have staff develop an operational plan and outline future upgrades for discussion at a workshop to be held shortly after the first of the year. Under the City Manager’s direction, staff has begun preparing a Master Plan that will be presented at the workshop. As part of this process, the City Manager, staff, and the consultant have conducted individual interviews with each City Commissioner to gather input on all aspects of the golf course and its operations. From these discussions, enhancements to the driving range emerged as a top priority.
Staff has identified a single-source vendor "Cover The Tees" with the specialized expertise and experience necessary to deliver the structural components of the driving range upgrades. This includes a high-performance canopy, integrated technology solutions, weatherproofing, preliminary design plans, and a preliminary site plan—provided as one comprehensive package using proprietary technology. These types of appurtenances provide options for both the serious golfer and non-serious golfer. Also, for the serious golfer, accommodations to hit on natural grass will be retained.
The vendor, which has constructed more than 80 similar driving ranges, including the facility at Dubsdread, offers a revenue-sharing model that requires no upfront capital investment. Timing is also critical, as a noncompete from another course in the area could prevent the City from securing this opportunity, potentially causing Forest Lake to lose its chance to be the first municipality in West Orange County to partner with this single-source provider, resulting in loss of market share and added time and cost of the project. Therefore, staff is requesting authorization to proceed with due diligence and negotiations of the agreement for approval at the January Commission meeting. The City's master planning efforts have optimized the potential location with respect to other community amenities at Forest Lake which will be discussed at the workshop.
title: Approve Staff to Negotiate a Single-Source Vendor Contract with Cover The Tees to Upgrade the Driving Range at Forest Lake Golf Club. (Parks and Leisure Services Director Johnson)

description:
In 2021, the City Commission approved a five-year contract with Central Florida Strategies for consulting services to support Legislative Affairs and Economic Development. Staff will be working closely with Central Florida Strategies on issues such as: i) Property Tax Reform, ii) Changes to Chapter 180 FL Statutes dealing with Live Local, iii) state and local transportation and infrastructure initiatives, and iv) Tourist Development Tax. As with the previous client consulting agreement, staff concludes that this arrangement provides significant value to the City based on several factors:
Hiring an employee to perform this work would cost roughly three times more with benefits and travel demands.
It would be challenging to find an employee with the necessary industry and legislative relationships required for this role.
It would also be difficult to find an employee with extensive knowledge of government operations in the metro Orlando area and statewide, combined with a strong understanding of private-sector land development financing.
These factors collectively support continuing the City’s successful partnership with Central Florida Strategies. Their expertise, regional insight, and established relationships have consistently delivered value that would be difficult and costly to replicate internally.
Accordingly, City staff recommends that the City Commission waive the purchasing code requirements and authorize the City Manager to execute the attached scope of services with Central Florida Strategies for a one-year term at an annual cost of $60,000, with the option for up to four additional one-year renewals.

The City of Ocoee is experiencing rapid growth and redevelopment, placing increasing demands on infrastructure and public services. Currently, individual departments rely on their own tools for maintenance and planning. This creates a fragmented approach that limits efficiency, response time, interdepartmental coordination, customer service, and long-term data-driven planning.
Brightly provides a unified asset management platform that consolidates all asset information (maintenance history, performance data, and asset location) into a single, centralized system, enabling comprehensive lifecycle asset management that includes planning, acquisition, maintenance, and disposal. It streamlines workflows and provides features like GIS mapping and mobile apps for inspections and maintenance. Brightly will provide transparency and better management of public roads, parks, sidewalks, buildings, and utilities.
Implementing Brightly will:Increase operational efficiency
Reduce costs through predictive maintenance and asset tracking
Improve the reliability and performance of city assets and extend the life of city assets
Support regulatory compliance
Strengthen financial planning and forecasting
Help us better serve our residents and businesses
Enable better management of public roads, parks, sidewalks, buildings, and utilities.
The implementation of Brightly City-wide is more than a system upgrade; it is a foundational strategic step that will define the future reliability and financial stewardship of the City of Ocoee. Its capabilities in predictive maintenance asset investment, and planning will enable us to deliver on our commitment to the community by creating safer, more reliable, and more sustainable infrastructure.
Staff is requesting approval to piggyback on the Omnia Contract # R 210702 for the implementation of Brightly asset management platform. Brightly has submitted a quote for implementation of the Brightly asset management platform in the amount of $133,686.05.
title: Approval to Piggyback Omnia's Contract for the Implementation of the Brightly Asset Management Platform. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
TNXL Academy Ducks LLC (TNXL) has submitted an unsolicited Letter of Intent (LOI) to purchase approximately 8.97 acres of land located at 1755 Adair Street (the Sorenson Field property), along with a 1.3 acre portion of 1701 Adair Street consisting of the strip of land situated between the Ison Center parking lot's east side and the existing TNXL facility. The parcels identified in the LOI are 08-22-28-2866-01-200 and 08-22-28-0000-00-041. Under the proposal, the Ison Center would retain 2.3 acres. The LOI offers a purchase price of $2,200,000 for the approximately 10.20 acres and includes TNXL’s commitment to replace the functionality of the two fields (sized for junior and senior level baseball) at Sorenson with like-sized fields at Vignetti Park —valued at roughly $900,000.
Founded in 2014 by Brian Martinez, TNXL Baseball Academy serves student-athletes in grades 6–12. Through its partnership with G3 Academy, TNXL provides a dual-pathway model that combines accredited academic instruction with high-level baseball training. The academy has established a strong track record of player development and placement, with 95% of graduates either signing collegiate baseball commitments or being selected in the Major League Baseball draft. In 2024, TNXL expanded its enrollment to 110 athletes and grew to four teams, which collectively captured the Premier Division Championship of the NAA Conference that same year.
On July 18, 2019, the City Commission approved a Lease Agreement with TNXL permitting construction of a baseball training facility and use of the fields at Sorenson Park. A subsequent First Amendment, approved on July 21, 2020, authorized construction of a permanent 80' × 120' building at the site. The Second Amendment, approved December 17, 2024, provided for a $640,000 capital investment by TNXL for facility improvements, including: (i) installing synthetic turf infields on both the Senior and Junior fields; (ii) raising the outfield fence on the Junior field; (iii) adding additional netting on the Junior field; and other enhancements. This amendment also reduced TNXL’s lease payments. The current lease rate is $1,500 per month with a 5% annual escalation. Per the agreement, the City maintains access to both Sorenson fields Monday through Friday from 5:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., and on Saturdays from 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. with 48 hours’ notice for City Little League and other municipal uses. Presently, under this agreement, the city reserves the fields for Legacy Charter School baseball team, Ocoee Middle School's feeder team to Ocoee High School, and various other travel ball teams. The City's Youth baseball league does not field any teams in the age bracket that would use the fields at this time.
TNXL’s submission of the LOI represents a significant step toward solidifying its long-term presence in Ocoee and supporting the continued expansion of its educational, training, and operational facilities. Ownership of the land and associated buildings would strengthen TNXL’s ability to secure capital investment and establish a more permanent foundation for future growth.
In November 2024, TNXL commissioned an appraisal of the combined properties, including the Sorenson Fields, the Ison Center building, and the existing TNXL facility under lease. The appraisal estimated the market value of the Sorenson Fields property at $675,000, and the combined value of the full acreage on the Ison Center property and both buildings at $2,337,000. A summary of the key elements of the LOI is provided below:
Purchase +/- 10.20 acres of land, including the two Sorenson ball fields, the land containing the existing TNXL building, and the additional land between that building and the Ison Center parking lot for $2,200,000.
Replace the functionality of the two fields at Sorenson with like fields at Vignetti Park.
Maintain City access to the Sorenson Fields—Monday through Friday from 5:00 p.m.–10:00 p.m., and on Saturdays from 8:00 a.m.–10:00 p.m. with 48 hours’ notice for City Little League and other uses—throughout the construction of the two Vignetti Park fields.
If the City Commission approves the LOI, staff will bring back a purchase and sale agreement to a City Commission meeting detailing the above terms and any other stipulations identified in the negotiations.
title: Unsolicited Letter of Intent (LOI) between TNXL Academy Ducks LLC and City of Ocoee for 10.20 +/- Acres of land located at 1755 Adair Street and 1701 Adair Street (Sorenson Fields and a portion of Ison Center property). (Assistant City Manager Rumer)

The Florida Interlocal Cooperation Act of 1969, Chapter 163, Florida Statutes, authorizes local governments to cooperate and jointly exercise powers through Interlocal Agreements. Additionally, Chapter 401, Florida Statutes, and Rule 64J-1.004, Florida Administrative Code, require all licensed Advanced Life Support (ALS) and Basic Life Support (BLS) providers to maintain a contract with a licensed physician to serve as Medical Director responsible for medical oversight, quality assurance, and supervision of emergency medical technicians (EMTs) and paramedics.
Orange County, through its EMS/Office of the Medical Director Division, employs a qualified physician to serve as the County’s Medical Director, currently Dr. Christian C. Zuver. The City of Ocoee Fire Department operates as an ALS transport agency under a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (COPCN) issued by Orange County and is required to maintain an Interlocal Agreement with the County for medical direction, quality management, and medical communications.
This Interlocal Agreement between Orange County and the City of Ocoee formalizes the City’s continued participation under the County’s Medical Director for EMS oversight and compliance. The agreement outlines the duties and responsibilities of both parties and satisfies all state and local requirements for maintaining ALS and BLS operations under County medical direction.

description:
The Ocoee Downtown Master Plan (2017) was developed through a six-month public process to shape the future of Ocoee’s historic downtown, nearby neighborhoods, and the lakefront. Within this comprehensive streetscape plan, the lack of sewer service was identified as a major hindrance to redevelopment, with septic tanks also significantly contributing to the nutrient loading of Starke Lake. Improvements along Bluford Avenue, including the installation of a new lift station and gravity sewer, were completed as the first phase of the project and provided the necessary connection points to expand central sewer service to the downtown area. With this framework established, expansion of the central sewer has continued. The Downtown Alleyway, Floral Avenue, and Cumberland Avenue projects have been completed. Oakland Avenue is nearing completion, and there are future sewer expansions planned over the next 5 to 10 years.
At present, forty-one customers in the downtown area have sewer service available but are not yet connected to the system. Parcels located within areas where sewer is available are required to connect pursuant to state law (Section 381.00655(1)(a), Florida Statutes) and as a condition of the 2016 Bond, which funded much of the downtown sewer construction. To assist customers with the cost of connection, the Utilities Department applied for and received a Florida Springs Protection Grant. This grant covers the construction costs on private property to connect to the sewer system. However, the grant does not cover the required sewer capital fee, which is mandated by the City Code and the 2016 Bond. The sewer capital fee is a one-time charge for all new connections to the sewer system that is paid by all new customers or new developments to cover the capital improvements costs associated with the addition of their new wastewater flow to the Ocoee Wastewater Treatment Plant.
As a condition of the Florida Springs Protection Grant, which provides up to $700,000 for customer construction costs, all forty-one parcels must connect to the sewer system and abandon their septic tanks no later than May 2028. Based on the current sewer capital fee, which increases annually on February 1, the fee for each residential home is $7,811. For commercial properties, the fee ranges from $7,811 to $48,050 depending on water use.
The typical cost for a residential home is $18,000 to $20,000 for construction of the sewer connection on their property (yard piping, abandonment of the septic tank, and restoration) and the required sewer capital fee. The grant reduces the customer’s cost by more than 50%. To best assist residents with the required capital fee, the Utilities Department is exploring payment options for the Commission’s consideration. One option is the use of a non-ad valorem tax assessment, which would allow customers to make installment payments through their tax bill. The tax assessment process requires advertisement for the Resolution of Intent to Use the Uniform Method of Collection for Non-Ad Valorem Special Assessment for four consecutive weeks prior to Commission action, with resolution adoption occurring before January 1, 2026. The Resolution of Intent to Use the Uniform Method of Collection for Non-Ad Valorem Special Assessment allows the Commission flexibility in the decision-making process for payment options to assist customers and does not obligate the Commission move forward with a tax assessment.
At this time, staff is requesting approval to advertise the Resolution of Intent to Use the Uniform Method of Collection for Non-Ad Valorem Special Assessment. The resolution must be advertised for a four (4) week period prior to this resolution being brought before the Commission. To meet the 2026 tax assessment and grant commitments, this resolution will be brought to the Commission on December 16, 2025.
title: Approval to Advertise Resolution of Intent to Use the Uniform Method of Collection for Non-Ad Valorem Special Assessment. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
The First Reading of the Ordinance was held on October 21, 2025.
Annually, the City is required to reconcile its budget at the close of each fiscal year. On December 11, 2024, the City Commission approved Ordinance 2024-28, adopting the budget for the fiscal 2024-25 fiscal year. Pursuant to Florida Statute 166.241 (8), the governing body of a municipality may amend the budget for a prior fiscal year at any time during that year or within 60 days following its conclusion. In accordance with this provision, the City Commission adopted a mid-year budget amendment through Ordinance 2025-05 on April 15, 2025.
Following a review of fund activities through September 30, 2025, Revenue and Expenditures exceeded what was budgeted and a subsequent budget reallocation and amendment is necessary prior to the fiscal-year close. This amendment will not raise the City’s millage rate, will have no impact on the overall financial position of the funds, and will address the deficit net position in the Sanitation Fund.
The General Fund increased due to the City receiving a FEMA reimbursement for Hurricane Ian and also incurred additional expenditures related to Hurricane Milton, specifically for debris monitoring services. An additional state contribution for police and firefighter retirement was received. A budget reallocation from the budget reserve is proposed to address increased expenses, including overtime pay in the Fire Department, retirement contribution in the Building division, and the one-time transfer to the Sanitation Fund to address its deficit net position.
Details of the Budget Adjustment and Allocation: Received FEMA reimbursement in the amount of $645,383 for hurricane recovery.
Additional $647,178 for Emergency & Disaster Expense in debris monitoring contract.
Received an additional $232,799 in State Retirement contribution for Police and Fire for public safety personnel:
$183,198 allocated to Police.
$49,602 allocated to Firefighter.
The Fire Department requires an additional $18,398 in additional funding for overtime expenses.
The Building Department requires an additional $3,000 in retirement contributions.
In September, the City Commission approved a one-time $1.3 million transfer to the Sanitation Fund to address its negative net position. Please note that the net increase in transfer-out is $885,047 with currently available to support this transfer. Therefore, the transfer will be limited to only $885,047.
Requesting an additional $350 transfer to the Debt Service Fund to cover the Agent Fee.
A total of $908,591 is proposed to be reallocated from the Budget Reserve to cover the additional expenses noted above.
Police Community Programs accounting to reflect increases in both revenue and expenses related to the Explorer and Community Affairs programs: $1,638 in donations received for the Explorer Program.
$960 donations received for the Community Affairs Program.
The Health Insurance Fund requires a budget true-up to show actual payroll contributions (City and employees), as well as the actual health claims and related costs incurred in the fiscal year. The total increase in both revenue and expense is $3,134,000.

description:
The property (parcel ID number 18-22-28-7122-01-250) is located within Commission District 3, is zoned RT-1 (Mobile Home Subdivision), and is within the Pioneer Key Park mobile home subdivision platted in 1976. It is bordered by road rights-of-way on the north, west, and south sides. Since the mobile home entryway faces west, the east side is considered the rear yard of the lot. Due to the narrowness of the lot, the mobile home cannot meet the minimum 20-foot rear setback. Therefore, the applicant is requesting a variance to reduce the minimum rear building setback from 20 feet to 7 feet, for the purposes of placing a 22’ by 36’ (792 square feet) mobile home on the lot.
The lot is a substandard lot of record, as it does not meet the minimum 7,000 square foot lot area for the RT-1 zoning district, but has retained the same configuration since the plat. Use of the lot for the installation of a mobile home is permitted subject to the home meeting all other applicable minimum zoning requirements, including building setbacks.
Provided below are the minimum zoning requirements for the RT-1 zoning district from Table 5-2: Minimum Zoning Descriptions on Permitted Uses. Side street setbacks are not currently indicated in Table 5-2. However, a 15-foot side street setback is intended to be made for residential zoning districts during the Land Development Code update, and the home meets the side street setback.

Per Article IV, Section 4-9A, approval of a variance requires that the applicant demonstrate compliance with four (4) criteria, as follows:That special conditions and circumstances exist which are peculiar to the land, structures, or required subdivision improvements involved and which are not applicable to other lands, structures, or required subdivision improvements;
That a literal interpretation of the provisions of these regulations would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties with similar conditions;
That the special conditions and circumstances do not result from the actions of the applicant;
That the granting of the variance requested will not confer on the applicant any special privilege that is denied by these regulations to other lands, structures, or required subdivision improvements under similar conditions. No pre-existing conditions of neighboring lands which are contrary to these regulations shall be considered grounds for the issuance of a variance.
Applicant Response: The applicant stated that the mobile home installer and property owner understood that they received approval for installation (Used Mobile Home Pre-Inspection Permit 3291-2024, attached). Money has already been invested in the project. We are requesting that setbacks be reconsidered for installation, specifically a 7-foot rear setback of the mobile home.
Staff Analysis: As a point of clarification, the mobile home "prior installation approval" (as documented in attachment 6) was the Building Division Inspection Report, which was a pre-inspection by the Building Inspector for purposes of the suitability of the mobile home structure for occupancy and was not City approval of the installation of the mobile home on the property.
Relative to the variance approval criteria, staff finds that, based on the circumstances and conditions of the existing lot, there is sufficient demonstration that the four (4) variance evaluation criteria are met. Staff analysis is summarized below:
Criteria 1: Special Circumstances & Conditions: The lot abuts road rights-of-way along three (3) property lines. Sunset Key Court abuts the lot on the north property line, and West Circle Key Drive abuts the lot on the south and west property lines. A boundary survey indicating the front yard, side street, and rear yard setbacks is attached based on the hierarchy of the roadway functions and the orientation of the mobile home. Applying the RT-1 zoning district minimum building setbacks to the lot would not permit the installation of a mobile home, as the minimum 20-foot rear setback (east property line) cannot be met.
Criteria 2: Literal Interpretation of Code: The literal interpretation of the provisions of these regulations would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties with similar conditions. Strict application of the front and rear minimum setbacks would result in a buildable area width of 10 feet, which cannot support a 22-foot wide mobile home.
Criteria 3: Actions of the Applicant: The circumstances of this variance are not the result of the actions of the applicant, as the lot has retained its original configuration since being platted in 1976. Due to the lot having three (3) frontages, the mobile home cannot meet the minimum 20-foot rear setback.
Criteria 4: Conference of Special Privilege: Approving the requested variance would not confer to the applicant any special privilege that is denied by these regulations to other lands, structures, or required subdivision improvements under similar conditions. Within Pioneer Key Park, there are existing mobile homes that were installed in accordance with the zoning regulations established prior to 1992. Approving the requested rear setback reduction would allow the property owner to install a mobile home on the lot like all the other lots in the mobile home subdivision, thus allowing the property owner the same benefit as other lots.
Additional Considerations:
As of 2011, twenty-eight (28) mobile home installation permits have been issued for properties in the Pioneer Key Park and Security Mobile Home Park subdivisions. Of the issued permits, a majority of the lots were conventionally rectangular interior lots that, despite not meeting the minimum lot area, met the setback requirements of the RT-1 zoning district.
For historical permitting purposes, the lot located at 40 Eagle Key Court has an identical configuration to 125 S. Circle Key Drive and was approved for a mobile home installation permit.
Staff supports the variance as there is sufficient justification to support the request.

description:
On April 1, 2025, the City Commission selected SSS Down To Earth OPCO LLC (DTE) to assume interim operations of the Forest Lake Golf Club. DTE was chosen from three qualified local vendors to manage the course from May 1, 2025, through November 3, 2025. A 30-day extension was later approved on October 7, 2025, extending operations through November 30, 2025.
After selecting an interim operator, the City issued RFP #25-006 to identify a long-term tenant to operate the Forest Lake Golf Club. The RFP opened publicly on August 5, 2025, and six responses were evaluated by the City’s RFP Evaluation Committee. On August 28, 2025, the Committee short-listed the following three firms:
• Hampton Golf Inc./FLGC Golf Holdings LLC
• Ocoee Golf Holdings, LLC
• Tamarack Golf Management, LLC
The City Commission approved the short-listed firms on September 16, 2025, and held a Special Session on October 21, 2025, to interview and receive presentations from each of them. Commissioner George Oliver was absent, but the Commission heard all three presentations and provided brief comments. The Mayor and the Commissioners present voted to continue the item to November 18, 2025, so that Commissioner Oliver could participate in the final vote.
Additionally, due to the continuation of the final selection, the Commission needs to further extend DTE up to 90-days which will bring the operations to March 31, 2026.
title: RFP # 25-006 for the Lease and Operation of the Forest Lake Golf Club. (Assistant City Manager Rumer)

description:
The Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) has awarded the Ocoee Fire Department $25,000 from the FY 2025–2026 Drone Replacement Grant Program. This program allows public safety agencies to replace non-compliant unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) with compliant models that meet the security requirements of Rule 60GG-2.0075, Florida Administrative Code.
The department is seeking permission to accept the grant funds and also to purchase one NDAA-compliant replacement drone kit per vendor Quote Q-43178 (dated September 28, 2025). The quote includes the compliant drone, accessories, support, and software, for a total of $25,087.15. The FDLE grant will provide $25,000, with the remaining $87.15 to be covered by existing Fire Department operational funds.
The new drone will enhance operational readiness for search and rescue, disaster assessment, structure-fire overwatch, and hazardous materials incidents, while ensuring compliance with Florida’s technology and cybersecurity requirements. The replacement aircraft will comply with Rule 60GG-2.0075, Florida Administrative Code.
OFD seeks to purchase the following equipment package from Skydio (Quote Q-43178, dated September 28, 2025):Skydio X10 Ready Kit with controller, case, batteries, chargers, and autonomy software
Skydio NightSense attachment (low-light operations)
Skydio Spotlight and Speaker
Skydio Care 1-year protection plan
Skydio Fleet Manager and Model Viewer subscription (12 months)
Skydio Connect 5G Range Extender (12 months)
Shipping
Total Project Cost: $25,087.15
Approval of this item will allow OFD to apply for a grant for one compliant aircraft and restore mission-critical aerial capabilities for structure fires, large-area searches, hazardous incidents, major events, and disaster assessments. An annual subscription cost of $120.00 will allow the department to utilize web based video streaming and flight/telemetry data.
title: Authorization to Accept FDLE Drone Replacement Program Grant Funding and Authorize the Purchase of a New Drone. (Deputy Fire Chief Van Camp)

description:
The Ocoee Fire Department (Department) is requesting authorization to purchase a 2026 E-One Typhoon Pumper fire engine. This apparatus is available for immediate acquisition, with anticipated delivery in spring 2026. The Department’s existing fleet of fire engines has reached advanced age, resulting in increased maintenance requirements, frequent mechanical failures, and prolonged periods of downtime. These issues hinder the Department’s ability to sustain dependable emergency response operations, as reduced fleet availability and escalating repair costs strain overall service capacity. Procuring a new 2026 E-One Typhoon Pumper will enhance operational reliability, ensure consistent emergency response readiness, and minimize disruptions caused by equipment breakdowns.
Industry standards recommend a service life of ten (10) years for front-line engines and an additional five (5) years in reserve status. The Department currently operates one engine nearing the end of its ten-year front-line service period and another reserve engine that is eighteen (18) years old. Approval of this purchase will enable the Department to continue its fleet modernization efforts by acquiring a semi-custom apparatus equipped with advanced, life-saving firefighting capabilities.
This fire engine acquisition was included in the Department’s Fiscal Year 2025–2026 capital improvement budget.
title: Approval of FY 2025-2026 Budgeted Fire Engine Purchase. (Deputy Fire Chief Van Camp)

description:

The grant funds 75 percent of the salary for a Victim Witness Advocate assisting the Ocoee Police Department. description:
The City’s water metering system (Sensus FlexNet®) currently uses the Sensus Customer Portal to provide customers with access to their detailed water usage data and custom alerts. This portal has been instrumental in enhancing customer service, reducing customer water use, and meeting the Consumptive Use Permit water use efficiency requirements established by the St. Johns River Water Management District and expanded water use efficiency requirements of the Central Florida Water Initiative.
Core and Main, the vendor for Sensus, notified the Utilities Department that the Sensus Customer Portal will be retired. Core and Main offers two customer portal solutions that are compatible with its data, with only one of these, VertexOne, meeting the City’s financial and operational needs.
VertexOne is a robust user-friendly customer portal platform, offering the same key features customers are used to—detailed usage history and alerts—as well as additional features such as strategic conservation tips and billing tools. Switching to VertexOne will enhance the customer experience by providing detailed usage and billing information, adding features such as leak alerts, usage analysis, billing cycle details, payment reminders, and conservation tips. The new platform will give the City greater transparency with customers. Moreover, its notification system should increase efficiency for Utility and Water Billing staff by reducing resident complaints and inquiries related to service suspension.
title: Approval to Contract Core and Main to Provide the VertexOne Customer Portal. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
The City of Ocoee’s Wastewater Treatment Permit requires that the City maintain a Sanitary Sewer Collections System Action Plan to prevent sewer overflows and wastewater leakages that may endanger public health and the environment. As part of this plan, the City is required to conduct pipe condition assessments on 10% of the gravity sanitary sewer system annually for the next 10 years starting in Fiscal Year 2025/26. This information is to be used in conjunction with other infrastructure performance indicators to identify, plan for, and complete repairs, replacements, maintenance activities, expansions, and upgrades to the sewer system. An annual report must be submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection by June 30, annually. This approach creates a long-term repair plan designed to improve capital planning by matching available funds and manpower and assisting staff with planning for grant opportunities.
RedZone Robotics specializes in wastewater infrastructure condition assessments using autonomous robots specially designed to overcome challenging underground pipe conditions. RedZone Robotics is the sole owner developer, and distributor of RedZone Robotics equipment, and their software includes AI predictive tools to better prioritize repair and replacements. GPS coordinates recorded during the assessment also provide the pipe's center line and manholes for GIS mapping.
The RedZone robot is the only product that requires fewer manhole access points, minimizing impacts on traffic flow in the area and limiting the need for extensive Maintenance of Traffic (MOT). The approved City of Ocoee Budget for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 includes a $120,000 budget for the condition assessment of 10% of the gravity sewer system (41,373 feet of linear pipe and 213 manholes). The Utilities Department has received a quote to inspect the first 10% of the total gravity system for a total cost of $94,959.66, $25,040.34 below the budgeted amount.
title: Approval of Red Zone Robotics to Complete the First Stage of Gravity System Condition Assessment. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
MPJ Realty USA, LLC (MPJ), a business that owns 3376 Seminole Street (Property), approached the City requesting water service for the Property. MPJ intends to make improvements consisting of a lot split and building two single-family residences. Addresses for this parcel after the lot split will be 3376 and 3206 Seminole Street.
The Property is currently located in Unincorporated Orange County, outside of Ocoee’s Joint Planning Area Boundary and City Limits and within the City's Water Service Territory. The City has an available water main directly north of the Property on Seminole St., which can be used to provide water service; however, the property owner must sign an intent to Annex for connection. Water service has already been provided under similar circumstances to the adjacent Property —3206 Seminole St—following a request from the owner (2004).
Staff worked with the City Attorney to modify the Standard Intent to Annex Agreement to address municipal boundary references and add the following language:
• The Owner agrees, upon request of the City, to apply for an amendment to the Joint Planning Area Agreement for the purpose of including the Property within the Joint Planning Area; and• The Owner agrees to not object to any amendment to the Joint Planning Area Agreement that would include the Property within the Joint Planning Area; and
MPJ must execute the modified Intent to Annex Agreement and pay all fees associated with the water connections and water service upfront and prior to any construction of the water services.
title: Approval of Intent to Annex Agreement with MPJ Realty USA, LLC. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description: The City of Ocoee contracted Hazen and Sawyer to design the above-ground injection assembly at the Forest Oaks Water Plant. The injection assembly is used to chlorinate the drinking water. The primary goal of this project was to eliminate the use of below-ground injection vaults, which pose a safety risk and are prone to leaks that are difficult to detect. During the survey of the underground piping at the water plant, it was determined that the existing piping layout requires modifications to accommodate the new assembly and future plant improvements necessary for additional supply and treatment. These issues necessitate correction and are compounded by impending regulations regarding PFAS and the need to expand the plant's treatment capabilities. The requested PO increase of $69,685.00 is necessary to expand the scope of design to modify the yard piping to allow for the required future expanded supply and treatment capabilities, accommodate expanded well capabilities, and provide construction sequencing guidelines to keep the plant in operation while still achieving the original objective of safely installing the new injection assembly and removing the hazardous subsurface vaults.
title: Approval of Amendment 1 for Hazen & Sawyer to Provide Additional Design Services for the Forest Oaks Above Ground Injection Assembly. (Utilities Director Bolling)

attachments.name: Ordinance for FY 2025 Year-End Budget Amendment

description:
Annually, the City is required to reconcile its budget at the close of each fiscal year. On December 11, 2024, the City Commission approved Ordinance 2024-28, adopting the budget for the 2024–25 fiscal year. Pursuant to Florida Statute 166.241(8), the governing body of a municipality may amend the budget for a prior fiscal year at any time during that year or within 60 days following its conclusion. In accordance with this provision, the City Commission adopted a mid-year budget amendment through Ordinance 2025-05 on April 15, 2025.
Following a review of fund activity through September 30, 2025, Revenue and Expenditures exceeded what was budgeted and a subsequent budget reallocation and amendment is necessary prior to the fiscal year-end close. This amendment will not increase the City’s millage rate, will have no impact on the overall financial position of the funds, and will address the deficit net position in the Sanitation Fund.
The General Fund increased due to the City receiving a FEMA reimbursement for hurricane Ian and also incurred additional expenditures related to hurricane Milton, specifically for debris monitoring services. An additional state contribution for police and firefighter retirement was received. A budget reallocation from the budget reserve is proposed to address increased expenses, including overtime pay in the Fire Department, retirement contribution in the Building division, and the one-time transfer to the Sanitation Fund to address its deficit net position.
Details of the Budget Adjustment and Allocation:
Received FEMA reimbursement in the amount of $645,383 for hurricane Ian recovery.
Incurred an additional $647,178 for Emergency & Disaster Expense within the debris monitoring contract.
Received an additional $232,799 in State Retirement contribution for Police and Fire for public safety personnel: $183,198 allocated to the Police.
$49,602 allocated to Fire.
The Fire Department requires $18,398 in additional funding for overtime expenses.
The Building Department requires an additional $3,000 in retirement contributions.
In September, the City Commission approved a one-time $1.3 million transfer to the Sanitation fund to address its negative net position. Please note that the net increase in transfer-out is $885,047, with $414,953 currently available to support this transfer. Therefore, the transfer will be limited to only $885,047.
Requesting an additional $350 transfer to the Debt Service Fund to cover the Agent Fee.
A total of $908,591 is proposed to be reallocated from the Budget Reserve to cover the additional expenses noted above.
Police Community Programs accounting to reflect increases in both revenue and expenses related to the Explorer and Community Affairs programs:
$1,638 in donations were received for the Explorer Program.
$960 donations received for the Community Affairs Program.
The Health Insurance Fund requires a budget true-up to show actual payroll contributions (City and employee), as well as the actual health claims and related costs incurred in the fiscal year. The total increase in both revenue and expense is $3,134,000.
title: First Reading of Ordinance for Fiscal Year 2025 Year-End Budget Amendment. (Assistant Finance Director Lawitzke)

description: The City was approached by the Tobacco Free Partnership of Orange County asking that we amend Chapter 124 of the Ocoee Code of Ordinances to address Vape and Vaping. description:
The Florida Department of Health administers the Emergency Medical Services Grant Program to assist local agencies in improving emergency medical services through the purchase of equipment, vehicles, and training resources. The Ocoee Fire Department intends to apply for funding through this program to replace expiring active shooter personal protective equipment (PPE). The application period to apply closes on November 30, 2025.
The Ocoee Fire Department’s ballistic vests and helmets are approaching the end of their 10-year service life and must be removed from operational use upon expiration. Replacing this equipment is necessary to maintain responder safety and operational readiness for potentially violent situations (PVS), active shooter incidents, and other hostile events where crews may operate in the “warm zone.”
The proposed replacement utilizes flexible rifle armor (FRAS®) and full-cut ballistic helmets that provide rifle-rated protection while reducing weight and increasing comfort and mobility. This modern configuration also integrates with communications, masks, and goggles, improving performance during joint operations.
Project Summary
Scope: Outfit frontline personnel and units with ballistic vests (flexible rifle armor) and helmets.
Operational Benefits:Greater flexibility and mobility (improved ergonomics for extended wear).
Less weight with equal or greater ballistic protection.
Increased protection against all handgun and common rifle rounds and other threats.
Enhanced integration with PPE for multi-agency interoperability.
The total project cost is $52,896.00. Under the program requirements, the City is responsible for a 25% matching contribution. This results in the following cost distribution:
Grant Award (75%): $39,652
City Match (25%): $13,244
title: Approval to Submit an Application for the Florida Department of Health Emergency Medical Services Grant for the Purchase of Active Shooter Equipment. (Deputy Fire Chief Van Camp)

description:
The Fire Department is requesting authorization to submit an application to the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) Drone Replacement Grant Program for a compliant public-safety drone and necessary operational accessories; to execute all related documents; and to take all actions necessary to accept and administer awarded funds.
The Fire Department purchased two drones in 2020 (DJI Mavic – $3,850; DJI Mini – $5,000). Due to State restrictions that were enacted well after the Fire Department purchased the drones, these aircraft are no longer permitted for operational use, leaving the department without an aerial situational awareness capability.
The FDLE's Drone Replacement Grant Program is currently accepting applications from all eligible first-responder agencies. The program provides up to $25,000 per compliant drone, including operationally necessary accessories. The replacement aircraft must comply with Rule 60GG-2.0075, Florida Administrative Code. OFD seeks to acquire the following equipment package from Skydio:
Skydio X10 Ready Kit with controller, case, batteries, chargers, and autonomy software
Skydio NightSense attachment (low-light operations)
Skydio Spotlight and Speaker
Skydio Care 1-year protection plan
Skydio Fleet Manager and Model Viewer subscription (12 months)
Skydio Connect 5G Range Extender (12 months)
Shipping
Total Project Cost: $25,087.15
This system meets FDLE compliance requirements and provides significant enhancements over prior capabilities.
Approval of this item will allow the department to apply for a grant for one compliant aircraft and restore mission-critical aerial capabilities for structure fires, large-area searches, hazardous incidents, major events, and disaster assessments. An annual subscription cost of $120.00 will allow the department to utilize video streaming and flight/telemetry data.
title: Authorization to Apply for Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) Drone Replacement Program Grant. (Deputy Fire Chief Van Camp)

description:
The Ocoee Police Department is seeking to transition from its current extra-duty software vendor, Extra Duty Solutions, to a new vendor, Off Duty Management Sourcewell. The benefits of the new software vendor include:
Enhanced Scheduling Capabilities – Off Duty Management provides additional scheduling software at no extra cost, including scheduling support for large-scale city events.
Cost Savings – The current vendor charges more than $3,000 annually for scheduling software, whereas Off Duty Management includes this service without additional fees.
Interagency Compatibility – Off Duty Management’s platform is compatible with other agencies’ systems, making it easier to coordinate schedules and ensuring faster payment processing. Extra Duty Solutions states that they could provide this service, but it would not be as efficient for the Ocoee Police Department or the Orlando Police Department.
Currently, extra-duty management is handled by an in-house staff member. By moving to Off Duty Management, the department will free up personnel from these administrative responsibilities. Staff will instead serve only as a liaison between the vendor, outside agencies, and the Ocoee Police Department.
title: Approval of the Off Duty Management Sourcewell Agreement. (Police Chief Ogburn)

description:
At its August 20, 2024, meeting, the City Commission approved the 2025 holiday schedule, which included the cancellation of four (4) regularly scheduled City Commission meetings. One of those dates, November 18, 2025, was canceled due to the anticipated attendance of one or more Commission members at the National League of Cities Conference. However, as no Commission member will be attending the conference, staff is now requesting to reinstate the regular City Commission meeting for November 18, 2025.
In addition, in light of a scheduling conflict, staff is requesting to cancel the regularly scheduled meeting on November 4, 2025, to allow members of the City Commission and the City Manager to participate in a targeted lobbying effort in Washington, D.C., alongside a coalition of cities named in H.R. 672 (Unified Zip Code) to be led by a federal lobbyist. This effort, scheduled for the evening of November 4th through 6th, will focus on meeting with U.S. Senators in support of H.R. 672.
At the May 5, 2025, City Commission meeting under the City Manager's announcements, the Commission authorized the City Manager to take all necessary actions to support H.R. 672, and participation in this advocacy trip is considered a critical step in advancing the City’s interests. As a refresher, H.R. 672 is a bill introduced in the 119th Congress (2025–2026) that seeks to establish new ZIP codes for several communities, including Ocoee. The bill has passed the House and is now under consideration by the Senate. To date, this represents the City’s most significant progress toward eliminating its five (5) ZIP codes and unifying all residents under a single ZIP code and Ocoee identifier.
title: Approval to Reinstate the November 18, 2025, City Commission Meeting and Approval to Cancel the November 4, 2025, City Commission Meeting. (Assistant City Manager Rumer)

description:
The Human Relations Diversity Board (HRDB) was established by resolution on September 16, 2003. Subsequent amendments to the resolution followed, with the most recent amendment providing for changes to membership and clarifying requirements as adopted by Resolution 2023-01 on January 17, 2023. The HRDB's general mission is to promote understanding, respect, goodwill, and equality among all citizens and businesses of the City of Ocoee. The board consists of seven (7) voting members: five (5) members are appointed by the City Commissioners, with each Commissioner selecting one member from their respective district, and the Mayor appointing one member from any district. Additionally, two (2) at-large members are chosen by the City Commissioners from a pool of eligible applicants who have submitted an application to serve on City Boards.
On August 15, 2025, the City Clerk's Department received an advisory board application from Reshell Smith, showing interest in the Human Relations Diversity Board, to fill the vacant member seat for District 2, with a term set to expire in May 2026. District 2 Commissioner, Rosemary Wilsen, has acknowledged Reshell Smith's application and directed the City Clerk's Department to move forward with presenting her application to the City Commission. There is still a vacant member seat for District 3 and to date, no other applications have been received by the City Clerk's Department.
title: Approval of District 2 Member Appointment to the Human Relations Diversity Board (HRDB). (City Clerk Sibbitt)

description: On August 7, 2025, Clarifier #3 at the City of Ocoee's Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) experienced a major mechanical failure, rendering it unable to operate as the backup to the City’s secondary clarification treatment process. Clarifiers are a crucial component of the wastewater treatment process, and it is vital to have 3 operational clarifiers available at all times for treatment redundancy and during extreme weather events. Staff reached out to Veolia Water Technologies (Veolia), the original designer of the WWTP and Sole Source vendor for the wastewater treatment plant parts for a repair quote. Veolia provided a quote of $62,460.43 for this emergency repair. Staff notified the City Manager of the expense for the emergency repair and authorized Veolia to schedule the repair after receiving approval from the City Manager.

description:
In compliance with the City of Ocoee (City) Purchasing Code Chapter 21, the City solicited proposals from qualified firms to perform all services identified in RFP #25-006 Lease and Operation of the Forest Lake Golf Club. For the purpose of securing a lease agreement with a qualified golf operator as the new tenant to operate, maintain, and market the city’s municipal golf course and related facilities known as Forest Lake Golf Club, which is comprised of an 18-hole championship golf course, driving range, practice green(s), maintenance facility and cart barn, clubhouse, golf shop, restaurant, and other related facilities and improvements, all as further specified and designated by the City, in the City’s sole discretion.
Forest Lake Golf Club originally opened in early 1995, Forest Lake encompasses 229 acres of Florida’s sandy ridges. This is one of the few Florida golf venues operating as a standalone course not associated with a resort or housing. The new tenant will be required to perform services including, but not be limited to: provide a high-quality golf experience with an emphasis on excellent course playability and exceptional customer service; properly maintain the golf course and all facilities to preserve and enhance the City’s investment: effectively and efficiently operate the Club golf operations, pro shop, restaurant, and grounds maintenance facilities to achieve acceptable profitability; market and promote the Club to increase market share and profit potential, including family and youth golf participation programs; develop and implement recommendations for a capital improvement master plan to update, enhance, and expand facilities to attract additional play and usage of clubhouse amenities.
The RFP was advertised on June 1, 2025, a Mandatory Pre-Proposal Conference was held on June 16, 2025, and the RFP was publicly opened on August 5, 2025. There were six (6) responses received. The City’s Owner’s Representative, Mr. Robert Utsey, Principal, ZHA Incorporated, and City Procurement Staff reviewed the proposals and all were considered responsive, see the attached Checklist. Attached are the six (6) responses, excluding financial statements which are confidential and exempt from public records.
The six (6) responses were evaluated by the RFP Evaluation Committee appointed by the City Manager, which consisted of five (5) members: Michael Rumer, Assistant City Manager; Michael Trent Hopper, Assistant Utilities Director; Mark Johnson, Parks and Leisure Services Director; Bob Doyle, PGA of America, Outside Expert Consultant; Scott Wellington, Senior Director, Section Business Operations, PGA of America, Outside Expert Consultant. The closed RFP Evaluation Committee meeting #1 Initial Discussions and Instructions and Negotiation Strategies was held on August 5, 2025. The public RFP Evaluation Committee meeting #2 was held on August 28, 2025, with the Evaluation Committee evaluating and shortlisting the firms on specific evaluation criteria. The Evaluation Committee short-listed the following three (3) firms in ranked order, and recommends the City Commission interview the top three (3) ranked firms, per the attached shortlist/evaluation form.
The next steps are to hold City Commission-led interviews of the Commission-approved shortlist and then to hold lease negotiations with the lease agreement subsequently brought back to the City Commission for approval. ​It is important to note that the Committee's recommendations are recommendations only and that the City Commission has final ​authority over the list of respondents who are granted an interview. ​

description:
On September 7, 2021, the City Commission approved on the Consent Agenda Resolution 2021-008 to Participate in Opioid Litigation Settlement as described in a Memorandum of Understanding between the State of Florida and local governments. The Memorandum of Understanding established a unified plan for allocating and using opioid settlement proceeds including for programming and services to expand the availability of treatment for individuals impacted by substance use disorders.
On September 17, 2021, the City approved on the Consent Agenda a Contingency Fee Agreement with the Romano Law Group and other affiliated law firms to represent the City of Ocoee in national litigation against opioid manufacturers. The Romano firm fronts litigation costs. in the litigation, the Romano firm and most other participating law firms agreed that, in lieu of charging a 20% contingency fee, they will accept payment from separate attorneys’ fee funds established as a part of each settlement. Ocoee and other local governments will keep 100% of the funds ultimately allocated to them. Attorney Eric Romano estimates that this will effectively reduce attorneys’ fees to approximately 8-10% of the amounts recovered.
Purdue Pharma marketed the pain medication OxyContin and, in 2019, filed for bankruptcy in response to numerous lawsuits. The City can participate in a proposed nationwide settlement agreement reached with Purdue (and certain of its affiliates) and its owners, the Sackler family, concerning alleged misconduct related to opioids.
Attorney Eric Romano has advised that the proposed Bankruptcy Plan will fund approximately $8 billion over 15 years to resolve opioid-related claims, including $6.5 billion from the Sackler family. He said the plan has broad support from all 50 states, representing a favorable resolution that will maximize funds available from Purdue and the Sackler family. The Disclosure Statement for Thirteenth Amended Joint Chapter 11 Plan of Reorganization of Purdue Pharma L.P. and its Affiliated Debtors, attached hereto, details the proposed settlement terms.
The United States Bankruptcy Court will hold a hearing to consider approval of the Bankruptcy Plan in November 2025. Mr. Romano submitted a proof of claim on Ocoee’s behalf, making Ocoee eligible to vote on whether to approve of the proposed settlement. Mr. Romano expects the settlement allocations to follow the model used in previous national settlements and the 2021 Memorandum of Understanding between the State of Florida and local governments.
To receive funds from the proposed Settlement, assuming approval by the Bankruptcy Court, the Mayor must sign a Participation Agreement.
On July 28, 2025, the City received formal notice of settlements with eight pharmaceutical companies or their affiliates — Alvogen, Inc., Amneal Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Apotex, Corp., Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc., Indivior Inc., Mylan N.V., Sun Pharma, and Zydus Pharmaceuticals U.S.A., Inc. The voluminous Settlement Agreements, available at: Additional Settlements – National Opioids Settlement, require:
Alvogen to immediately pay up to approximately $19 million;
Amneal to pay up to approximately $74 million over 10 years, and to provide either approximately $177 million of its generic version of the drug Narcan or up to an additional approximately $44 million in cash;
Apotex to immediately pay up to approximately $65 million;
Hikma to immediately pay up to approximately $98 million, and to provide either approximately $35 million of its naloxone product or up to an additional approximately $7 million in cash;
Indivior to pay up to approximately $75 million over five years, a portion of which, at the election of the state, could be paid in the form of Indivior’s branded buprenorphine and/or nalmefene products with a value of up to $140 million.
Mylan to pay up to approximately $290 million over nine years;
Sun Pharma to immediately pay up to approximately $32 million; and
Zydus to immediately pay up to approximately $15 million.
In sum, the settlements will provide $844 million in cash payments and $355 million in medications for treating opioid addiction and reversing overdoses. Local governments will have an option to convert a portion of the medications into $87 million in additional cash. The Settlement Agreement also consents to injunctive relief severely restricting each company’s future opioid sales and marketing.
To participate in the settlements, the City of Ocoee must “opt in.” Again, to receive funds from the proposed Settlement, the Mayor must sign a Participation Agreement. The deadline to sign and return the required documentation is October 8, 2025.
title: Approval to Opt In the Opioid Litigation Settlement and Receive Funds. (City Attorney Geller)

description:
The Ocoee Fire Department provides structural firefighting services and is required to maintain compliant, high-quality personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure the safety and effectiveness of its personnel during emergency operations. As part of its ongoing effort to ensure firefighter safety, the Department conducted a comprehensive evaluation of several leading bunker gear manufacturers. The evaluation considered critical criteria including cost, NFPA compliance, thermal protection, durability, ergonomic design, serviceability, and overall long-term value.
Following this review, Morning Pride, manufactured by Honeywell First Responder Products, was determined to be the most cost-effective solution while meeting the Department’s operational and safety requirements. Morning Pride equipment exceeds the NFPA 1971 standard and is recognized for its performance, comfort, and protective capabilities.
In order to promote consistency in PPE across the department and streamline future procurement, the Fire Department is requesting to standardize bunker gear ensembles, including helmets, jackets, and pants, to Morning Pride and designating it as the sole source provider for this equipment.
Sourcewell is a nationally recognized cooperative procurement agency that has already competitively solicited and awarded contracts in compliance with public sector purchasing laws. The City currently has a registered Sourcewell account.
To facilitate this purchase, the Department will utilize the Sourcewell cooperative purchasing contract #010424-MNP. Utilizing this contract enables the City to benefit from volume-based pricing and reduce administrative overhead while ensuring procurement compliance.
title: Approval to Purchase Firefighting Bunker Gear Ensembles from Morning Pride via Sourcewell and Designate Morning Pride as a Sole Source Provider. (Deputy Fire Chief Van Camp)

The PBA Union has proceeded to a ratification vote of the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreements (by the sergeants and police officers). As the police officers have voted 44 in favor and 4 against the terms and the sergeants have voted 9 in favor and 0 against the terms for ratification, the City Commission is required to vote to approve the Collective Bargaining Agreements as ratified by the members of the PBA.
In light of prevailing market volatility, the City’s bargaining team and the PBA agreed to implement a wage adjustment for Year 1 of the contract only. Additionally, both parties consented to a wage re-opener clause for Years 2 and 3 to allow for renegotiation based on future economic conditions and fiscal considerations. Communities seeking funding from the Resilient Florida Program must be endorsed by their governing body.
The City recently participated in Orange County’s efforts to update their Vulnerability Assessment and found there is a need for the City to update its GIS inventory of critical assets, establish a Citywide Vulnerability Assessment, and implement projects addressing needs found in the County’s Vulnerability Assessment update and subsequent City Vulnerability Assessment. Public Works recommends endorsing the above eligible planning and implementation projects under the Resilient Florida Program within the Office of Resilience and Coastal Protection.

description:
The attached Resolution provides support for the Community Contribution Tax Credit Program (CCTCP) which was established as part of the Florida Department of Commerce to encourage private sector participation in community improvement and housing projects. The program offers tax credits to businesses that have made donations to approved community organizations. Approval of this resolution by the City Commission does not designate any entity as an eligible sponsor. Each entity with a project located in the City of Ocoee must obtain its own resolution for that specific project. This would result in the entity attending a City Commission meeting for its own resolution adoption after being vetted by the City Manager's Office.
The Community Contribution Tax Credit Program (CCTCP) provides a financial incentive (up to 50% tax credit or sales tax refund) to encourage Florida businesses to make donations toward community development and housing projects for low-income persons. Businesses located anywhere in Florida that make donations to approved community development projects may receive a tax credit of up to 50 percent of the value of the donation. Businesses may take the credit on Florida corporate income tax, insurance premium tax, or as a refund against sales tax if the business is registered to collect and remit sales taxes with the Department of Revenue (DOR).
Non-profit organizations and units of state and local governments may apply to become eligible sponsors and solicit donations under the program.
title: Approval of Resolution Expressing Support for the Community Contribution Tax Credit Program (CCTC) Authorized under 212.08(5)(p) FL Statutes. (Assistant City Manager Rumer)
