description:
The Public Works Fleet Division routinely utilizes local vendors for specialized diagnostics and repairs. The City's Fire Department Engine #25, a 2016 model, has experienced an engine failure. Fleet sent the truck to Rush Truck Center of Florida, Inc., the local Cummins engine service dealer, who confirmed the engine had met the end of its useful service life and required rebuilding. The remainder of the apparatus on the truck continues to function without issues and the vehicle is not scheduled for replacement in the immediate future. The estimated cost of the engine rebuild is $49,022.83, which is below the City Manager's approval threshold per the Purchasing Manual. However, adding to the cost of previous diagnostics in the current fiscal year for other vehicles has raised the total expenditures with Rush Truck Center to $60,577.50, which now requires Commission approval for single source expenditures.
Public Works is seeking approval from the City Commission to designate Rush Truck Centers as a single source vendor for the Fleet Division, to serve as the local service dealer for Cummins engines. The cost proposals from Rush Truck Centers align with industry standards for diagnostics and repairs. Public Works recommends the approval of Rush Truck Centers as a single source vendor in accordance with the City's Purchasing Manual.
title: Approval of Rush Truck Centers of Florida, Inc., as Single Source Vendor. (Public Works Director Krug)

description:
Chapter 163, Part II, Florida Statutes, requires that local governments adopt a comprehensive plan that establishes the principles, guidelines, standards, and strategies for the orderly and balanced economic, social, physical, environmental and fiscal development of the City. Section 163.3177(5)(a), F.S., requires that the Comprehensive Plan includes at least two planning periods, one covering at least the first 10-year period occurring after the plan’s adoption and one covering at least a 20-year period.
The current Comprehensive Plan, adopted on October 1, 2002, has reached its long-term planning horizon of 2022. Therefore, "The Comprehensive Plan must be updated to include the statutorily required ten-year and twenty-year planning horizons." Additionally, Section 163.3177(6), F.S., requires the Comprehensive Plan to be based on relevant and appropriate data and an analysis by the City that may include, but not be limited to, surveys, studies, community goals and vision, and other data available at the time of the preparation and adoption of the plan.
To maintain compliance with Chapter 163, Part II, Florida Statutes, the City is moving forward with and is actively preparing its Comprehensive Plan, entitled "Envision 2045 Ocoee Comprehensive Plan" ("Envision 2045"), which shall be the governing policy framework to direct growth and development in the city over the next twenty years. Envision 2045 shall establish Goals, Objectives, and Policies to achieve its vision of Ocoee becoming “a vibrant, attractive and economically sustainable community where businesses thrive and neighborhoods flourish through diverse, compact, and complementary land uses that produce quality developments, enhanced and active public realms, and safe and efficient mobility systems while simultaneously preserving environmental systems and creating parks, trails and open spaces to promote social engagement, community health and overall well-being of the City."
Envision 2045 and its supporting Data, Inventory and Analysis (DIA) document are being prepared in-house by a multi-department Comprehensive Planning Team comprised of staff from Development Services, Public Works, Utilities, and Parks and Leisure Services, with technical assistance from the City's transportation consultant firm regarding the Transportation Element (which will be renamed the Mobility Element). The DIA document, upon completion, will contain an evaluation of historical growth and development trends. It will also include the development of the City's 2045 population projections based on several methodologies (including those listed in Florida Statutes), an evaluation of anticipated demands, and an assessment of the City's ability to accommodate these demands on public infrastructure and municipal services, including completion of the 10-Year Water Supply Plan. The Comprehensive Planning Team has prepared a Vision Statement for Envision 2045 and drafted Goals and Objectives for each of the required Elements. Team members continue to work diligently on developing the implementing policies for Envision 2045 and finalizing the DIA document, in addition to performing their regular duties and responsibilities.
Concurrently with Envision 2045's preparation, Development Services staff, with technical assistance from the Comprehensive Planning Team, is updating the Land Development Code to create zoning districts, urban design and architectural standards, development policies and procedures, and other regulations to implement the Goals, Objectives, and Policies of Envision 2045. The LDC Update is an 18-month contract with a Planning Consulting Firm that kicked off in February 2024. The first LDC Draft Deliverable, received on December 31, 2024, was rejected by the City for incompleteness, and Development Services staff have met with the Consultant on several occasions to develop an acceptable First Draft. Staff anticipates that completion of the LDC Update will occur after the completion of Envision 2045 Comprehensive Plan. Based on current tracking, the completion of Envision 2045 Comprehensive Plan is as follows:
Planning and Zoning Commission Workshop - March 20, 2025
Planning and Zoning Commission Hearing - April 8, 2025
City Commission 1st Reading Transmittal - April 15, 2025
State Agencies 45-Day Commenting Period - May 30, 2025
City Commission 2nd Reading/Adoption - June 17, 2025
Therefore, the completion of the new Land Development Code update will have both the 1st and second reading/adoption in July 2025.
The attached Resolution puts the public and all parties on notice that the City is actively preparing its new governing policy framework embodied within Envision 2045 and new and updated Land Development Code to bring nonconformities into compliance, to govern real properties, including buildings, structures and premises, as necessary, to protect the health, safety and welfare of existing and future residents and property owners within the City’s jurisdictional limits, and to foster development patterns and designs that not only protect but also enhance the public realm with beautiful peacemaking standards, that promote the efficient use of municipal investments and infrastructure, that achieve infill, redevelopment and adaptive reuse, and that add to the quality, character, economic vitality, and sustainability of the City, and includes provisions for the City's enforcement.
The City wishes to give notice that it is implementing the Pending Legislation Doctrine (also known as the Pending Ordinance Doctrine) concerning Envision 2045 and updated Land Development Code governing real properties within the City limits. Any land development applications submitted after the moratorium on processing expires on March 17, 2025, shall be subject to Envision 2045 and the new Land Development Code. Such submissions may include applications: (a) to amend the Comprehensive Plan text or Future Land Use Map; or (b) to rezone land in the City; or (c) to obtain special exception allowing certain use(s) on land in the City; or (d) for preliminary or final site plan or subdivision approval.
title: Approval of Resolution of Pending Legislation to Provide for New Governing Policy Framework and Land Development Regulations. (Zoning Manager Whitfield)

In accordance with Section C-50 of the Ocoee City Charter, the Canvasing Board will consist of the City Clerk and two (2) citizens appointed by the City Commission. The City Commission shall also appoint two (2) additional citizens to serve as alternates to the Canvassing Board. On February 5, 2013, the consensus of the Commission was that the Mayor and two (2) Commissioners whose district seats are not part of the election should each select members for the Canvassing Board. In keeping with that practice, Mayor Johnson, Commissioner Kennedy and Commissioner Firstner would each need to appoint members to the Canvassing Board.
During the City Commission Meeting on February 4, 2025, Mayor Johnson and Commissioner Firstner announced their appointments, and the City Commission made a motion to approve the appointments of Lincoln Forges and Derrick Chacon as regular members, and Sharon Duffy as an alternate member of the 2025 Canvassing Board. Commissioner Kennedy indicated that he would propose his appointee at a later time. On February 5, 2025, Commissioner Kennedy submitted Jason Mellen as his appointee to the 2025 Canvassing Board. Mr. Mellen will serve as one of the two alternate members.
title: Appointment of an Alternate Member to the 2025 Canvassing Board. (City Clerk Sibbitt)

description: Ocoee Little League has been a staple in the community for over 50 years. However, in recent years, the league has faced increasing competition from private, travel-baseball teams, leading to a decline in participation. As a result, recruiting volunteers to administer/operate the league has become a challenge. In response, the Ocoee Little League Board approached the City, requesting that city staff take over league operations, as the board had planned to dissolve. Without City involvement, the league is at risk of complete collapse. Taking over the program should be seamless, as the Little League Board will transfer $12,666.19 to the City, and annual revenues (listed under financial impacts) should easily exceed the costs of continuing this program within our community. Staff reached out to other municipalities that have successfully taken over struggling little leagues, and all have reported positive outcomes.
title: Approval for the City to Take Control of Ocoee Little League Operations. (Parks and Leisure Services Director Johnson)

The Original MOU enabled the mutual sharing of an encryption key to access certain Orange County encrypted Metro radio channels among the original parties. The City of St. Cloud, including St. Cloud Police Department, has requested access to the encryption key to enable it to access the Orange County encrypted Metro radio channels. description: The City of Ocoee annually budgets funds to repair and seal manholes and lift stations with an impervious protective coating on a rolling maintenance schedule. This preventative maintenance is a proactive best practice that limits the structural decay that occurs over time and is crucial to ensuring the longevity of the utility system. Atlantic Pipe Services provided the most competitive pricing for these projects by allowing the City to piggyback off Volusia County's contract for "Coatings for Wet Well and Manholes". This competitive pricing has enabled Utilities to contract Atlantic Pipe Services for three separate projects this year, and staff have been very satisfied with both the product and the application. The combined total for the work performed by Atlantic Pipe Services exceeded the $50,000.00 purchasing threshold requiring any additional work to have Commission approval.
title: Approval to Piggyback Volusia County Contract for Coatings for Wet Well and Manholes with Atlantic Pipe Services. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description: The City of Ocoee residential and commercial water rates consist of a base charge and inclining usage rates to promote water conservation. These rates are periodically reviewed to ensure that they are sufficient to cover all operating and capital expenses involved in providing continued reliable water, sewer, and reclaimed water services, as well as regulatory compliance. Raftelis Financial Consultants, Inc. (Raftelis) has consistently provided multiple departments within the City with comprehensive financial studies. Raftelis has a proven track record with the City and has in-depth knowledge of City financial practices and projects, and provided a quote of $51,600.00 to perform a utility revenue study. The study will include a full report detailing their findings and suggestions, which would require further action from the City Commission to adopt any approved rate changes.
title: Approval to Contract Raftelis Financial Consultants, Inc. to Perform a Water, Wastewater, and Reclaimed Water Revenue Sufficiency Study. (Utilities Director Bolling)

Establish maximum intensity for the activity center via specific uses and a maximum floor area ratio of 0.4 in lieu of the 4.0 allowed within the Commercial FLU designation,
Establish a maximum of 17,960 net new external daily trips irrespective of adjustments in the development program and
Formalize owner/developer commitments that would run with the land in perpetuity for transportation, utilities, and other infrastructure improvements needed to accommodate the proposed development of the Northwest Activity Center.
Development of the Ocoee Regional Sports Complex within the Northwest Activity Center includes removal and disposal of the contaminated soil on the Brownfield, dedication of land to the City for a new city park and associated parking, extension of 17th Avenue to connect North Lakewood Avenue to Ocoee Apopka Road to improve east-west travel and several transportation improvements. Additionally, through the widening of Ocoee Apopka Road, connectivity with the West Orange Trail will be achieved and promoted. The entire site will be designed with the need for connected pedestrian/bicycle access and safety and the ability of emergency services to move about the project site in mind.

The proposed development is anticipated to generate over 9,800 construction-related jobs, over 5,100 permanent jobs in the retail, hospitality, restaurant, sports and entertainment, and professional office industries, as well as tourism-related jobs and economic opportunities.
Consistency with JPA Agreement: Parcels 07-22-28-0000-00-039, -041, -043, -074, and -105 were annexed into the City in June 2024 without an initial zoning classification. Thus, these five (5) parcels currently have the County's A-1 zoning classification and are designated Low Density Residential (LDR) on the Joint Planning Area (JPA) Agreement Future Land Use Map (FLUM). A prerequisite to amending the City's FLUM in the Comprehensive Plan, the FLUM of the JPA must first be amended and approved by both the City and the County. To this end, the City Commission has approved the Fourth JPA Amendment, and said Fourth JPA Amendment has been sent to the County and is scheduled to go before the Orange County Board of County Commissioners on March 20, 2025. Per the Traffic Impact Analysis, the proposed access points are as follows:Along Ocoee Apopka Road (5 access points): one (1) signalized full access driveway, one (1) full access unsignalized driveway, two (2) limited access unsignalized driveways plus the new intersection of Ocoee Apopka Road and 17th Avenue Extension,

The TIA was prepared based on methodology developed in accordance with the approved TIA Methodology from the City's concurrency management system and in coordination with City staff. Based on the TIA, there are no roadway segments that are operating below the proposed CPA and development program will result in several roadway segments and intersections anticipated to operate below the adopted level of service standards. The TIA also evaluated possible mitigation options and listed recommendations for improvements aimed at creating capacity as well as improving intersection operations and vehicular movement. Per the proposed text amendment, "the owner/developer shall be responsible for improvements to transportation, utilities, or any other infrastructure associated with the project's development, as specified in the applicable Land Use Plan(s), Development Agreement(s), Conditions of Approval, or equivalent legal instruments." Consequently, the above-listed improvements will be included as transportation commitments within a new Development Agreement binding on the properties within the Northwest Activity Center at Ocoee Apopka Road and Fullers Cross Road boundary.
Utilities: The Utilities Department has indicated that, based on the proposed development program and projected demands, water and wastewater treatment capacity are available at the respective treatment plants. Points of connection to the City's system shall be assessed during the preliminary site plan review. The City continues to evaluate reclaimed water offsets needed for compliance with the City's Consumptive Use Permit (CUP) with the St. Johns River Water Management District. The closest point to reclaimed water is a 12-inch reclaimed main located north of State Road 429 on Ocoee Apopka Road. The Utilities Department continues to work with the water/sewer/reclaimed water designer to accurately quantify utility demands and has provided to the applicant team a series of comments and conditions of approval that are to be used for the preparation of the Land Use Plan and Preliminary Site Plan.
Stormwater: The subject property is located within the Ocklawaha River Basin (which includes the Lake Apopka Drainage Basin) and the Wekiva Recharge Protection Basin, and, as such, drainage and stormwater design shall be subject to the engineering and protection criteria of each basin. To mitigate impacts from the use of fill within the 100-year FEMA floodplain, compensatory storage for drainage shall be required to accommodate approximately 8.03 acres of impacted floodplain on-site and 0.82 acres of impacted floodplain off-site (within the right-of-way). A Letter of Map Revision (LOMR) shall be sought, and no fill shall be used within the floodplain prior to the approval of FEMA and the City.
Environmental Analysis:
Wetlands and surface waters. The subject property contains wetlands, a man-made canal and Basinger Sand and other fine sands that are well-draining. The CPA proposes to convert the entire site to a Commercial FLU designation, and the proposed development program will impact approximately 32.3 acres of Conservation-designated land. The applicant conducted a UMAM evaluation on the 32.3 acres to evaluate the quality of the wetlands. The UMAM, or Uniform Mitigation Assessment Method, is the Florida Department of Environmental Protection's "standardized procedure for assessing the ecological functions provided by wetlands and other surface waters, the amount that those functions are reduced by a proposed impact, and the amount of mitigation necessary to offset that loss". The UMAM also determines "the degree of improvement in ecological value of proposed mitigation bank activities". Based on the UMAM, the 32.3 acres of Conservation area contains approximately 21.94 acres of wetlands. The UMAM Evaluation showed that the three (3) wetland areas on the site are low quality wetlands with ratings between 3 and 5 out of 10 per evaluation criteria (connectivity, water quality and vegetative community structure). Of the 21.94 acres of wetland area, approximately 9.34 acres of "total functional units" would be impacted per the UMAM.
While Policy 6.2 of the Conservation Element requires that there remains a minimum 25-foot upland buffer adjacent to wetlands and the ecological community, this policy and other policies within the Conservation Element also allow alternative wetland protection and mitigation strategies when wetland impacts are unavoidable. Specifically, CON Policy 4.1(c) states "where alteration or removal of wetlands is necessary in order to allow reasonable development of property, either the restoration or enhancement of disturbed wetlands will be provided or additional wetlands will be created to mitigate any wetland destruction, within the same site or watershed, if possible."
CON Policy 4.3 states “where disturbance is permitted, requiring a two-for-one replacement of area, maintenance of proximal relationship and functionality, and enforcement of alternative mitigation requirements become necessary.”
CON Policy 6.2 states “comprehensive mitigation measures where environmental impacts are unavoidable.”
The above provisions on wetlands impacts and mitigation are also reflected in Section 7-4B(1) through (5), Part I, Article VII of the Land Development Code.
Based on the 9.34 acres of impact and the required 2:1 remediation ratio, the applicant would need to provide approximately 18.68 acres of equivalent quality wetlands area (9.34 acres of functional units loss x 2). Due to the limited availability of land that would meet the provisions of Policy 4.3, the applicant has instead opted to provide a combination of wetland replacement and a mitigation strategy pursuant to Policy 6.2. Specifically, in an effort to achieve consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code, the applicant has committed to (1) preserving, via dedication to the City, a 9.9-acre vacant wooded parcel which is designated Conservation on the Future Land Use Map and which contains wetlands, and (2) establishing a Monitoring and Maintenance (M&M) Plan for the restoration and maintenance of approximately 287.82 acres of conservation lands (comprised of 277.92 acres of Conservation lands owned by the City plus the 9.9-acre to-be-dedicated property).
The Public Works Department found that the M&M Plan is acceptable and has requested that a UMAM Evaluation be prepared for both the 9.9-acre to-be-dedicated property and the 277.92 acres of City-owned properties in order to establish a baseline of the existing conditions on these properties as supporting documentation for the Monitoring & Maintenance Plan. During the DRC meeting, the applicant team concurred with this request. Furthermore, the applicant/developer has agreed to establish a perpetual funding mechanism for the conservation M&M Plan covering the 287.82 acres of conservation land. The applicant's environmental consultants have attested at the Development Review Committee (DRC) meeting that the proposed mitigation plan satisfies requirements of other agencies.
Flora and fauna. An assessment for listed flora and fauna species was conducted at the site on March 21 and 26, 2023, and June 6 and 7, 2023. The work included both direct observations and indirect evidence, such as tracks, burrows, tree markings, and vocalizations, which indicated the presence of the species observed. Various flora and fauna species were observed on the site. The assessment found that no plant species listed as "Threatened" or "Endangered" by either the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (DACS) or U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) were identified during the assessment. However, three (3) species identified on the site are listed as "commercially exploited" by DACS. These species are Cinnamon Ferm, Royal Fern, and Saw Palmetto. According to DACS, commercially exploited species may be removed for development activity but may not be harvested, transported, or sold for commercial gain. Furthermore, though there is a potential for the presence of protected fauna species (such as Gopher Tortoise, Bald Eagle, Indigo Snake, and Wood Stork), no presence of these protected species was observed during the field assessments. The environmental analysis recommends another field assessment at least 90 days prior to construction to ensure no Gopher Tortoises or their burrows are present. Bald Eagle nest identified as OR045 was not present during the June 2023 field assessment, and no other Bald Eagle nests were observed. The applicant noted that the Audubon EagleWatch determined nest OR045 to be "unknown" for the 2022 nesting season. No Wood Stork rookeries were observed. To yield a no net loss of potential Wood Stork foraging habitat, the stormwater management, and littoral shelves within the stormwater management ponds would likely produce a larger foraging habitat than will be impacted.
Schools: The proposed Amendment will eliminate student demand for school capacity as the previous residential entitlements will be replaced with this commercial development.
Public Safety: The property will be served by Ocoee emergency services.
section: SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE – PUBLIC HEARING
title: Second Reading and Public Hearing of an Ordinance for Ocoee Regional Sports Complex Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map (FLUM) Amendment from Low Density Residential (LDR) and Conservation (CON) to Commercial (COMM) and Corresponding Text Amendment to the Future Land Use Element; Project No. CPA-2024-006. (Zoning Manager Whitfield)

description:
The First Reading of the Ordinance was held at the February 4, 2025, City Commission Meeting.
Request: The applicant is requesting to amend approximately 150.9 acres of land from City PUD (95.11 acres), City R-1AA (38.01 acres) and County A-1 (approximately 17.78 acres) to City PUD for purposes of developing the Ocoee Regional Sports Complex.
Owner/Applicant: The developer/owner is Jaime Douglas, MDTL Enterprise/Owner, as represented by Marcos Bastian, AECOM, the applicant. However, the proposed Ocoee Regional Sports Complex (ORSC) is a partnership project between the City and Montierre Development, PLLC. In 2022, the City partnered with Montierre Development to facilitate the development of the ORSC, a proposed 150-acre multi-use project, in an effort to generate substantial economic benefits for the residents of Ocoee and for the public in the region by creating thousands of jobs in various industries and delivering on the City's continued commitment to create attractive and connected places for residents and the public to dine, shop, work, gather, and recreate.
General Location: The subject property is within Commission District 3 and is generally located in the southeast corner of the intersection of Ocoee Apopka Road and Fullers Cross Road.
Property Size and Parcel ID No.: The subject property consists of nine (9) parcels totaling approximately 150.9 acres, assigned parcel identification numbers 07-22-28-0000-00-001 (the Chevron Property), 07-22-28-0000-00-023, 07-22-28-0000-00-057, 07-22-28-0000-00-041, 07-22-28-0000-00-039, 07-22-28-0000-00-043, 07-22-28-0000-00-105, 07-22-28-0000-00-060, and 07-22-28-0000-00-074.
Existing Site Conditions: The table below summarizes the existing conditions of the property.

The property is within the Lake Apopka Drainage Basin, which is within the Ocklawaha River Basin. A large portion of property contains contaminated soils and has been designated a Brownfield.

The LUP also proposes several waivers to the Land Development Code (LDC) as follows: Waiver to Article VIII Sign Code to allow signage for the project to be regulated per a Master Sign Plan to be developed, reviewed and approved as part of the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process.
Waiver to Sections 6-7 Surface Water Management and 6-10 Landscaping requirements to allow flexibility in the design of drainage easements, open drainage ways, drainage maintenance berms and landscaping plan at the time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process, which by Code includes a public hearing process.
Staff Analysis: The findings of staff's evaluation of the proposed rezoning are provided below.
1) Stormwater: The subject property is located within the Ocklawaha River Basin (which includes the Lake Apopka Drainage Basin) and the Wekiva Recharge Protection Basin, and, as such, drainage and stormwater design shall be subject to the engineering and protection criteria of each basin. To mitigate impacts from the use of fill within the 100-year FEMA floodplain, compensatory storage for drainage shall be required to accommodate approximately 8.03 acres of impacted floodplain on-site and 0.82 acres of impacted floodplain off-site (within the right-of-way). A Letter of Map Revision (LOMR) shall be sought, and no fill shall be used within the floodplain prior to the approval of FEMA and the City. Stormwater management design will be evaluated at the time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process and engineered/finalized at the time of Final Site Plan review.
2) Utilities: Potable water, reclaimed water, and wastewater utilities will be provided by the City of Ocoee. Points of connection to the City's system shall be assessed during the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review. The Utilities Department continues to evaluate reclaimed water offsets needed for compliance with the City's Consumptive Use Permit (CUP) with the St. Johns River Water Management District. The closest point to reclaimed water is a 12-inch reclaimed main located north of State Road 429 on Ocoee Apopka Road. The Utilities Department continues to work with the water/sewer/reclaimed water designer to accurately quantify utility demands and has provided to the applicant team a series of comments and conditions of approval that are to be used for the preparation Preliminary Site Plan. In addition to the conditions of approvals listed on page 2 of 13 of PUD plan set, the Utilities Department has requested the following:Revision of the Development Sequencing Plan to add a note stating that all relocations and extensions of public utilities shall be completed with Sequence 01/Phase 01;
Addition of a Condition of Approval stating that the developer shall assume maintenance responsibility, including the costs of any maintenance, repair, or FDEP fines, for the portion of the Commerce 429 project's 4-inch force main located on this project site. The Developer shall assume maintenance responsibility for the entirety of the mass grading and site work, and such responsibility shall terminate when the Site Certificate of Completion (CoC) is issued for the final sequence/phase of the project.
Revision to the Conceptual Utility Plan to add a note stating that all City utilities shall be located in the public right-of-way or a utility easement and to correct the location of the existing 4-inch force main serving Commerce 429 (per the as-builts provided to the applicant team).
Either revise the Development Sequencing Plan to include phasing of utilities or revise the Conceptual Utility Plan to show a phasing/sequencing plan that is consistent the Development Sequencing Plan.
3) Transportation / Traffic: A traffic impact analysis (TIA) for the maximum 17,960 net external daily trips (per adopted text amendment) was performed during the review/approval of the Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map and Text Amendment (CPA). The TIA identified the study network, existing and anticipated deficiencies and needed transportation improvements, including roadway capacity improvements (i.e. widening of Ocoee Apopka Road and extension of 17th Avenue) and intersection and driveway improvements. Commitments for transportation improvements were addressed/documented in the CPA submittal. Design and engineering of the needed transportation improvements will be at time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan submittal and review. Timing/phasing and details of construction will be developed in a Development Agreement. Per the adopted text amendment, "the owner/developer shall be responsible for improvements to transportation, utilities, or any other infrastructure associated with the project's development, as specified in the applicable Land Use Plan(s), Development Agreement(s), Conditions of Approval, or equivalent legal instruments."
4) Schools: N/A
5) Public Safety: Fire, police and other emergency services will be provided by the City of Ocoee. Conditions of approval relative to public/life safety, including the preparation of an Emergency Plan, to be approved by the Fire and Police Departments, at time of Preliminary Site Plan submittal, are incorporated in the Conditions of approval (also on page 2 of 13 of the LUP plan set). Fire and Police Department staff have provided the below concerns and comments:Heights of multi-story buildings and structures (7 to 10 stories) continue to be a concern as Ocoee Fire Department is unable to protect that tall of a structure. The Fire Department will need at least a 100-foot to 110-foot dual axel ladder truck.
Relative to fire protection for the proposed parking garages, the Fire Department will need a blitz type vehicle to extinguish vehicle fires inside the structures as the fire engines are too tall to enter parking/garage structures. Additionally, standpipe/sprinklers will be needed in the parking garages.
The Fire Department remains concerned about fire access/life safety issues, as outlined below, that will need to be worked out during the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review:Limited access to some of structures due to the water feature and parking layout.
Evaluation of the access road that is being proposed in order to ensure that all of the Fire Department's vehicles can utilize it without significant issues, i.e. sufficient room for fire engines/units to turn around, maneuver, ingress/egress safely, etc.
Evaluation of each component of the development, i.e. hotel, parking garages, retail buildings, etc.
Additional EMS components that function within the property may be needed, including one to two ruggedized EMS golf carts (gas operated), one fully stocked EMS treatment room, potentially one EMS substation (depending upon the location of the primary EMS treatment room), and AED/AED towers strategically located throughout the property.
Water supply throughout the project/hydrant-standpipes.
Additional fire protection may be needed if delayed access/response is expected (i.e. fire sprinklers/fire alarm).
Consideration must be given to alternative suppression cart/vehicle for interior structures.
EMS station or stations at specified locations to house rescue/supplies, etc.
Provision of AEDs throughout the project site.
Provision/assurance of additional fire safety personnel during large events.
Preparation of an Emergency Management Plan, along with a Crowd Manager monitoring overcrowding during entertainment events.
Bridges to be used for Fire Department access may be needed. The Emergency Management Plan must also include a strategy for ensuring that emergency shelters or other safe areas are available so that players, spectators, and other patrons can take refuge safely during inclement weather, i.e. lightning and severe rain delays.
A condition that the Ocoee Fire Department shall be the only entity approved to provide and manage the Emergency Medical System (EMS) within the development and property.
Ocoee Fire Department's current ambulance fleet will not suffice if there are a significant amount of EMS calls generated by the growth in this sector of the city. An additional rescue ambulance and associated equipment (Life pack monitor, stretcher, Power load system, Lucas device, staffing, etc.) will be needed to transport patients.
6) Wetlands: Impacts were evaluated as part of the Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map and Text Amendment. Based on the 9.34 acres of anticipated impact and the required 2:1 remediation ratio, the applicant would need to provide approximately 18.68 acres of equivalent quality wetlands area (9.34 acres of functional units loss x 2). Due to the limited availability of land that would meet the provisions of Policy 4.3 of the Conservation Element, the applicant will provide a combination of wetland replacement and a mitigation strategy pursuant to Policy 6.2 of the Conservation Element. Specifically, to achieve consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code, the applicant has committed to (1) preserving, via dedication to the City, a 9.9-acre vacant wooded parcel which is designated Conservation on the Future Land Use Map and which contains wetlands, and (2) establishing a Monitoring and Maintenance (M&M) Plan for the restoration and maintenance of approximately 287.82 acres of conservation lands (comprised of 277.92 acres of Conservation lands owned by the City plus the 9.9-acre to-be-dedicated property).
A Monitoring and Maintenance (M&M) Plan was provided to Public Works, and they have found it to be acceptable. The applicant will need to conduct a UMAM Evaluation of the 9.9-acre Conservation Tract and the 277.92 acres of City-owned lands that are covered by the M&M Plan and will need to establish a perpetual funding mechanism for the implementation of the M&M Plan covering the 287.82 acres of conservation land.
7) Recreation and Open Space: Not required as there are no proposed residential units; however, the LUP includes a dedication of two (2) acres of land for the development of a city park.
8) Joint Planning Area (JPA) Agreement: A Fourth Amendment to the JPA has been approved by the City Commission on February 4, 2025 to amend the future land use designations of the seven (7) properties annexed into the City in May 2024 from Low Density Residential (LDR) to Commercial (COM). attachments.name: Ordinance for Tree Removal Permits (Strike-outs and Underlines ) - Second Reading
Business Impact Estimate Form - Ordinance Updating Chapter 45, Arbor Code

description:
First Reading of the Ordinance was held on January 7, 2025.
On November 7, 2023, the Ocoee City Commission placed a moratorium on tree removal permit requests by Homeowners Association (HOA) or Property Owners Association (POA) in the form of a blanket tree removal permit to remove more than one (1) tree in a private right-of-way, landscape buffer, or common open space. Also, based on a new State law passed in 2022, the Florida legislature amended Section 163.045, Florida Statutes, to limit the circumstances under which the owners of residential property can remove trees without a permit and to require, at the time of tree removal, possession of documentation of an onsite Tree Risk Assessment report meeting industry standards signed by a certified arborist or licensed landscape architect declaring that a tree posed a moderate, high, or extremely high risk to persons or property.
On March 5, 2024, the Ocoee City Commission directed staff to evaluate and develop standards for tree pruning and maintenance, especially as they relate to street trees and utility lines.
Thus, staff is proposing an amendment to Chapter 45, Arbor Code, and Chapter 163, Trees on Public Lands, within the Code of Ordinances. The following provides an overview of the amendment and highlights changes from the first reading.
Updates the definition of "protected tree" clarifying that a protected tree is eight inches or greater and includes newly planted trees required to meet Land Development Code or planted as replacement trees.
Clarifies and revises regulations relative to tree removal requirements, including application, review process, and determination of just cause.
Provides a process for City Commission review of tree removal applications in residential developments to maintain the landscape aesthetic of each community. Language has changed since First Reading to remove the reference to “private” only and add a process for compliance with Code for all residential communities and subdivision right-of-ways, landscape buffers, parking areas, and common open space areas.
Establishes regulations related to tree removal in conformance with Section 163.045, Florida Statutes, including a requirement for providing the City with a copy of any Risk Assessment report, prepared by a certified arborist or licensed landscape architect, that lead to the removal of a tree, within 10 dates of removal.
Provides regulations on tree pruning for tree branches that overhang streets and sidewalks.
Lists prohibited pruning activities and techniques.
As it pertains to number 5 above, the amendment addresses the minimum clearance for tree branches, providing for clear travel on roads and safe passage on sidewalks, and public ways; regardless if the road or sidewalk is within a private development or not. On a related note, City staff is in the process of developing tree and landscape maintenance standards that will be followed by our staff and landscape maintenance contractors.

description:
As part of the approved City of Ocoee Budget for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, the Water Field Capital Improvement budget includes $70,000.00 to replace the communication base station for the Sensus FlexNet® Water Metering System. The communication base station is the radio read system that collects customer consumption data from the City's smart water meters and transmits this data for utility billing. Base stations have a typical life span of 10 years. This base station is the oldest of the City's three (3) stations, was installed in 2010, and utilizes outdated technology that has reached the end of its useful life.
Core & Main, who is the sole source provider of Sensus products, has provided a quote of $72,340.02 to install a new base station that is supported by a five-year protection plan. While this is higher than the budgeted amount, Staff was able to realize savings on other capital improvement projects and apply those funds to cover the overage for this project.
title: Approval to Replace the Base Station for the Sensus FlexNet Metering System. (Utilities Director Bolling)

attachments.name: FY24-25 Locke Well & Pump Purchase Orders with Competitor Quotes

description: The City of Ocoee’s water treatment plants use wells to extract water from the Floridan Aquifer and, after the water is treated, High Service Pumps (HSP) are used to pump treated water into the City’s water distribution system. The Utilities Department utilizes a rolling 10-year maintenance plan to schedule and budget well inspections and fund the repair or replacement of pumps, motors and other appurtenances used to maintain the City of Ocoee’s potable water supply. There are a limited number of contractors with the necessary qualifications to provide well inspections and make required repairs. For several years, Locke Well & Pump has consistently provided the lowest bid for well inspections & equipment against other qualified contractors (Florida Armature Works, PSI Technology, Power & Pump, Mader Electric and CMS Florida) and provide outstanding service when needed. As such, the City of Ocoee has issued purchase orders totaling $79,184.45 with Locke Well & Pump this fiscal year, which brought the cumulative total over the City Manager’s approval level of $49,999.99.
title: Approval of Locke Well & Pump as the Single Source Vendor for Well Inspections, Repairs and Equipment. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
The City of Ocoee Utilities Department currently operates and maintains seventy wastewater lift stations that collect and pump sewage from their respective areas to the City’s wastewater treatment plant. During widespread power outages and extreme weather events, the Utilities Department deploys five mobile generators to combat power outages at the wastewater lift stations and avoid catastrophic failures. During preventative maintenance, generator #959, a 19-year old generator, experienced a total mechanical failure. Due to the advanced age of the now inoperable generator, repairs are both cost prohibitive and unreliable. Staff recommends upgrading the replacement generator with a 100-kilowatt unit that can provide backup power supply redundancy by also meeting the high-power demands at the City’s larger wastewater lift stations. The upgraded generator provides emergency backup power supply and supports the Utilities Department ongoing resiliency efforts.
The City is a member of the Sourcewell, a cooperative purchasing agency that has the legal authority to do national solicitations or national bids for competitive pricing. A replacement mobile generator is available for purchase under Sourcewell Contract #09222-CAT at a total cost of $103,470.58
title: Approval to Piggyback Sourcewell Cooperative Purchasing Contract to Replace a Mobile Generator. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
Request: The applicant is requesting to amend approximately 150 acres of land from City PUD (95.11 acres), City R-1AA (37.11 acres) and County A-1 (approximately 17.78 acres) to City PUD for purposes of developing the Ocoee Regional Sports Complex.
Owner/Applicant: The developer/owner is Jaime Douglas, MDTL Enterprise/Owner, as represented by Marcos Bastian, AECOM, the applicant. However, the proposed Ocoee Regional Sports Complex (ORSC) is a partnership project between the City and Montierre Development, PLLC. In 2022, the City partnered with Montierre Development to facilitate the development of the ORSC, a proposed 150-acre multi-use project, in an effort to generate substantial economic benefits for the residents of Ocoee and for the public in the region by creating thousands of jobs in various industries and delivering on the City's continued commitment to create attractive and connected places for residents and the public to dine, shop, work, gather, and recreate.
General Location: The subject property is within Commission District 1 and is generally located in the southeast corner of the intersection of Ocoee Apopka Road and Fullers Cross Road.
Property Size and Parcel ID No.: The subject property consists of nine (9) parcels totaling approximately 150 acres, assigned parcel identification numbers 07-22-28-0000-00-001 (the Chevron Property), 07-22-28-0000-00-023, 07-22-28-0000-00-057, 07-22-28-0000-00-041, 07-22-28-0000-00-039, 07-22-28-0000-00-043, 07-22-28-0000-00-105, 07-22-28-0000-00-060, and 07-22-28-0000-00-074.
Existing Site Conditions: The table below summarizes the existing conditions of the property.
Current Future Land Use (FLU) Map DesignationCurrent Zoning DistrictExisting Land UseOverlays/Unique FeaturesCommercial (150 acres)PUD-LD, R-1AA and County A-1Most of parcels are vacant, partially wooded lots; a few are occupied by single-family dwellingWetlands, man-made canal, and Basinger, other hydric fine sandy soils. The property is within the Lake Apopka Drainage Basin, which is within the Ocklawaha River Basin. A large portion of property contains contaminated soils and has been designated a Brownfield.
The property is surrounded by the following: jurisdictions, Future Land Use Map designations, zoning districts and existing land uses.

Proposed Land Use Plan: The applicant proposes to change the zoning classification of approximately 150 acres of Commercial FLUM designated property from City PUD, City R-1AA, and County A-1 zoning to City PUD. As part of the PUD rezoning, a Land Use Plan (LUP) establishing the development parameters for that specific PUD is required. The table below summarizes the proposed Land Use Plan for the PUD.
Proposed Zoning ClassificationProposed UseProposed Development ProgramPlanned Unit Development (PUD)Multi-sport sports complex, hotel, indoor/outdoor entertainment, restaurant, retail, office and assembly/conference uses and associated infrastructureIn accordance with the adopted text amendment, development on the property is limited to:42 acres of sports fields & entertainment venues,

The development will be served by an amenitized, pedestrian-activated stormwater "riverwalk" and surface, podium, and garage parking.
Inclusive of parking facilities, the maximum development is 2.46 million SF.
The LUP proposes the below development standards for development on the property:

Entertainment: 1 space for each 250 GSF

Hotels: 1 space for each hotel key, plus 1 space for each 3 employees (1 employee for every 4 keys)
Assembly/conference: 1 space for each 250 GSF

The LUP also proposes several waivers to the Land Development Code (LDC) as follows: Waiver to Article VIII Sign Code to allow signage for the project to be regulated per a Master Sign Plan to be developed, reviewed and approved as part of the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process.
Waiver to Sections 6-7 Surface Water Management and 6-10 Landscaping requirements to allow flexibility in the design of drainage easements, open drainage ways, drainage maintenance berms and landscaping plan at the time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process, which by Code includes a public hearing process.
Staff Analysis: The findings of staff's evaluation of the proposed rezoning are provided below.
1) Stormwater: The subject property is located within the Ocklawaha River Basin (which includes the Lake Apopka Drainage Basin) and the Wekiva Recharge Protection Basin, and, as such, drainage and stormwater design shall be subject to the engineering and protection criteria of each basin. To mitigate impacts from the use of fill within the 100-year FEMA floodplain, compensatory storage for drainage shall be required to accommodate approximately 8.03 acres of impacted floodplain on-site and 0.82 acres of impacted floodplain off-site (within the right-of-way). A Letter of Map Revision (LOMR) shall be sought, and no fill shall be used within the floodplain prior to the approval of FEMA and the City. Stormwater management design will be evaluated at the time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review process and engineered/finalized at the time of Final Site Plan review.
2) Utilities: Potable water, reclaimed water, and wastewater utilities will be provided by the City of Ocoee. Points of connection to the City's system shall be assessed during the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review. The Utilities Department continues to evaluate reclaimed water offsets needed for compliance with the City's Consumptive Use Permit (CUP) with the St. Johns River Water Management District. The closest point to reclaimed water is a 12-inch reclaimed main located north of State Road 429 on Ocoee Apopka Road. The Utilities Department continues to work with the water/sewer/reclaimed water designer to accurately quantify utility demands and has provided to the applicant team a series of comments and conditions of approval that are to be used for the preparation Preliminary Site Plan. In addition to the conditions of approvals listed on page 2 of 13 of PUD plan set, the Utilities Department has requested the following:Revision of the Development Sequencing Plan to add a note stating that all relocations and extensions of public utilities shall be completed with Sequence 01/Phase 01;
Addition of a Condition of Approval stating that the developer shall assume maintenance responsibility, including the costs of any maintenance, repair, or FDEP fines, for the portion of the Commerce 429 project's 4-inch force main located on this project site. The Developer shall assume maintenance responsibility for the entirety of the mass grading and site work, and such responsibility shall terminate when the Site Certificate of Completion (CoC) is issued for the final sequence/phase of the project.
Revision to the Conceptual Utility Plan to add a note stating that all City utilities shall be located in the public right-of-way or a utility easement and to correct the location of the existing 4-inch force main serving Commerce 429 (per the as-builts provided to the applicant team).
Either revise the Development Sequencing Plan to include phasing of utilities or revise the Conceptual Utility Plan to show a phasing/sequencing plan that is consistent the Development Sequencing Plan.
3) Transportation / Traffic: A traffic impact analysis (TIA) for the maximum 17,960 net external daily trips (per adopted text amendment) was performed during the review/approval of the Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map and Text Amendment (CPA). The TIA identified the study network, existing and anticipated deficiencies and needed transportation improvements, including roadway capacity improvements (i.e. widening of Ocoee Apopka Road and extension of 17th Avenue) and intersection and driveway improvements. Commitments for transportation improvements were addressed/documented in the CPA submittal. Design and engineering of the needed transportation improvements will be at time of Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan submittal and review. Timing/phasing and details of construction will be developed in a Development Agreement. Per the adopted text amendment, "the owner/developer shall be responsible for improvements to transportation, utilities, or any other infrastructure associated with the project's development, as specified in the applicable Land Use Plan(s), Development Agreement(s), Conditions of Approval, or equivalent legal instruments."
4) Schools: N/A
5) Public Safety: Fire, police and other emergency services will be provided by the City of Ocoee. Conditions of approval relative to public/life safety, including the preparation of an Emergency Plan, to be approved by the Fire and Police Departments, at time of Preliminary Site Plan submittal, are incorporated in the Conditions of approval (also on page 2 of 13 of the LUP plan set). Fire and Police Department staff have provided the below concerns and comments:Heights of multi-story buildings and structures (7 to 10 stories) continue to be a concern as Ocoee Fire Department is unable to protect that tall of a structure. The Fire Department will need at least a 100-foot to 110-foot dual axel ladder truck.
Relative to fire protection for the proposed parking garages, the Fire Department will need a blitz type vehicle to extinguish vehicle fires inside the structures as the fire engines are too tall to enter parking/garage structures. Additionally, standpipe/sprinklers will be needed in the parking garages.
The Fire Department remains concerned about fire access/life safety issues, as outlined below, that will need to be worked out during the Large-Scale Preliminary Site Plan review:Limited access to some of structures due to the water feature and parking layout.
Evaluation of the access road that is being proposed in order to ensure that all of the Fire Department's vehicles can utilize it without significant issues, i.e. sufficient room for fire engines/units to turn around, maneuver, ingress/egress safely, etc.
Evaluation of each component of the development, i.e. hotel, parking garages, retail buildings, etc.
Additional EMS components that function within the property may be needed, including one to two ruggedized EMS golf carts (gas operated), one fully stocked EMS treatment room, potentially one EMS substation (depending upon the location of the primary EMS treatment room), and AED/AED towers strategically located throughout the property.
Water supply throughout the project/hydrant-standpipes.
Additional fire protection may be needed if delayed access/response is expected (i.e. fire sprinklers/fire alarm).
Consideration must be given to alternative suppression cart/vehicle for interior structures.
EMS station or stations at specified locations to house rescue/supplies, etc.
Provision of AEDs throughout the project site.
Provision/assurance of additional fire safety personnel during large events.
Preparation of an Emergency Management Plan, along with a Crowd Manager monitoring overcrowding during entertainment events.
Bridges to be used for Fire Department access may be needed. The Emergency Management Plan must also include a strategy for ensuring that emergency shelters or other safe areas are available so that players, spectators, and other patrons can take refuge safely during inclement weather, i.e. lightning and severe rain delays.
A condition that the Ocoee Fire Department shall be the only entity approved to provide and manage the Emergency Medical System (EMS) within the development and property.
Ocoee Fire Department's current ambulance fleet will not suffice if there are a significant amount of EMS calls generated by the growth in this sector of the city. An additional rescue ambulance and associated equipment (Life pack monitor, stretcher, Power load system, Lucas device, staffing, etc.) will be needed to transport patients.
6) Wetlands: Impacts were evaluated as part of the Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map and Text Amendment. Based on the 9.34 acres of anticipated impact and the required 2:1 remediation ratio, the applicant would need to provide approximately 18.68 acres of equivalent quality wetlands area (9.34 acres of functional units loss x 2). Due to the limited availability of land that would meet the provisions of Policy 4.3 of the Conservation Element, the applicant will provide a combination of wetland replacement and a mitigation strategy pursuant to Policy 6.2 of the Conservation Element. Specifically, to achieve consistency with the Comprehensive Plan and Land Development Code, the applicant has committed to (1) preserving, via dedication to the City, a 9.9-acre vacant wooded parcel which is designated Conservation on the Future Land Use Map and which contains wetlands, and (2) establishing a Monitoring and Maintenance (M&M) Plan for the restoration and maintenance of approximately 287.82 acres of conservation lands (comprised of 277.92 acres of Conservation lands owned by the City plus the 9.9-acre to-be-dedicated property).
A Monitoring and Maintenance (M&M) Plan was provided to Public Works, and they have found it to be acceptable. The applicant will need to conduct a UMAM Evaluation of the 9.9-acre Conservation Tract and the 277.92 acres of City-owned lands that are covered by the M&M Plan and will need to establish a perpetual funding mechanism for the implementation of the M&M Plan covering the 287.82 acres of conservation land.
7) Recreation and Open Space: Not required as there are no proposed residential units; however, the LUP includes a dedication of two (2) acres of land for the development of a city park.
8) Joint Planning Area (JPA) Agreement: A Fourth Amendment to the JPA will be needed to amend the future land use designations of the seven (7) properties annexed into the City in May 2024 from Low Density Residential (LDR) to Commercial (COM). These properties are parcel ID numbers 07-22-28-0000-00-074, 07-22-28-0000-00-105, 07-22-28-0000-00-039, 07-22-28-0000-00-041, 07-22-28-0000-00-043, 07-22-28-0000-00-057, and 07-22-28-0000-00-060. It is anticipated that this Rezoning and the Fourth JPA amendment will be presented to the City Commission on February 4, 2025, for a First Reading of the Rezoning application and approval/adoption of the JPA Amendment in anticipation of the CPA and Rezoning ordinances being presented to the City Commission for their respective Second Readings/Public Hearings on February 18, 2025.

section: SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE – PUBLIC HEARING
title: SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE – PUBLIC HEARING
PUBLIC HEARING

description:
The property is located in Commission District 3 and addressed at 304 Calliope Street. It is zoned R-1AA (Single Family Dwelling District) and is assigned parcel ID number 32-22-28-9285-00-740. Per Section 5-14A and corresponding Table 5-2 (Minimum Zoning Descriptions on Permitted Uses) of Article V of the Land Development Code, the maximum allowable impervious surface area (ISA) for all lots within all residential zoning districts is 50% of the lot area. The property contains 9,380 SF of land area, thus, the maximum ISA permitted is limited to 4,690 SF. The applicant is requesting a total ISA of 7,558.53 SF (or 81% of the lot), representing a 61.2% variance to Table 5-2. This causes the lot to exceed the maximum allowable impervious surface area (ISA) by 31% (approximately 2,907.80 SF) for purposes of installing impervious surface materials in the rear and side yards, specifically:Installation of pavers covering nearly the entirety of the rear yard, and
Installation of paver walkways along the side yards.
According to Article IV, Section 4-9A, approval of a variance requires that the applicant demonstrate compliance with four (4) criteria, as follows:That special conditions and circumstances exist which are peculiar to the land, structures, or required subdivision improvements involved and which are not applicable to other lands, structures, or required subdivision improvements;
That a literal interpretation of the provisions of these regulations would deprive the applicant of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties with similar conditions;
That the special conditions and circumstances do not result from the actions of the applicant; and
That the granting of the variance requested will not confer on the applicant any special privilege that is denied by these regulations to other lands, structures, or required subdivision improvements under similar conditions.
Applicant Response: The applicant's justifications are as follows:
This project involves the installation of pavers in the backyard of a residence in Ocoee, Florida. Specifically, this variance request seeks the City’s approval for an increase in the maximum allowable impervious area percentage for the property. The installation of pavers covers the entire patio area and is intended to address a rodent control issue (rats). The current total area of the pavers in the backyard patio is approximately 2,876 square feet. The survey titled “Proposed Survey for 2024 Permit” illustrates the total proposed paver area.
The primary motivation for this intervention is to address the presence of rats and snakes on the property, which have emerged due to the proximity and operation of a sewer pump located behind the residence, belonging to Thornebrooke Elementary School. The implementation of pavers aims to provide an effective and long-lasting solution to the pest problems.
Pest Control: The presence of rats and snakes in the backyard area, exacerbated by the presence of the sewer pump, indicates a public health and safety concern. Installing pavers can help create a surface that limits hiding spots for these animals, thereby reducing their presence.
Enhancement of Safety: By reducing hiding spots for rats and snakes, the safety of the residence is increased. This is especially important for the family and neighbors with children and pets, who are more vulnerable to dangerous encounters.
Stormwater Management: In addition, pavers allow water to filter through their joints, which helps reduce runoff and minimizes the risk of flooding. This contributes to better management of rainwater and protects the surrounding environment. By allowing water to filter through the joints of the pavers, it contributes to sustainable water management.
Finally, the lot has a natural slope that allows for effective drainage of rainwater without affecting neighboring properties, as the water flows toward the back of the residence. During the heavy rains associated with Hurricane Milton, it was clear that the rainwater filtered through the pavers, preventing any accumulation in the neighboring residences. Additionally, most of the pavers have been installed since 2020, which demonstrates that during the various storms experienced in Florida, characterized by substantial rainfall, the natural drainage created by the slope of our patio has successfully mitigated water accumulation and drainage issues.
Staff Analysis: Staff finds that the justifications provided by the applicant do not support and are not sufficient to demonstrate compliance with the four (4) evaluation criteria. Staff's analysis is summarized below:Criteria 1: Special Circumstances & Conditions: There are no special conditions and circumstances that exist that are peculiar to the land in that the subject lot is of similar dimensions, shape, and size as all of the lots in this block of the subdivision. The lot is rectangular in shape with a slight bend along the East property line near the front of the lot. Also, like all of the lots in the subdivision, the subject lot has 5-foot drainage and utility easements along the side lot lines where impervious materials are not permitted.
Criteria 2: Literal Interpretation of Code: The literal interpretation of the provisions of these regulations would not deprive the property owner of rights commonly enjoyed by other properties with similar conditions. Construction of the residence (including the front covered porch and rear covered lanai), driveway, and walkway yielded an ISA of approximately 43%, leaving approximately 7% (or 656.6 square feet) of impervious surface area available for use by the property owner. The remaining 7% (or 656.6 square feet) of impervious surface area coverage allows adequate square footage for the property owner to construct a reasonably sized patio or other accessory structures on the property.
Criteria 3: Actions of the Applicant: The circumstances of this variance are the result of the actions of the applicant/property owner. The property was cited by Code Enforcement for having unpermitted pavers in the rear and side yards. In an effort to be compliant with Code Enforcement, the applicant/property owner pursued a building permit to account for the 1,922 square feet of existing unpermitted pavers installed in 2020 plus the desired additional 1,569.25 SF of pavers to the property (refer to the attached survey).
Criteria 4: Conference of Special Privilege: Granting the requested variance would confer a special privilege to the applicant that is denied by these regulations to other lands or required subdivision improvements under similar conditions, as other properties are also not permitted to exceed the maximum ISA.
On December 16, 2024, staff met with the applicants to discuss their issues and concerns relative to rodents and snakes in their backyard; however, staff explained that the variance criteria do not speak to nuisance-related concerns and clarified that the variance would not constitute approval of impervious materials (pavers) within the Drainage and Utility Easements. The applicants agreed to reduce the width of the paver walkways along the sides of the residence from 3 feet wide to 2.48 feet wide so as to not encroach into the easements. This will reduce the impervious area by 97.24 square feet, or 1%, bringing the total requested ISA to 80%.
Staff does not support the requested variance as there is insufficient, code-based justification to support the variance.
title: Public Hearing for 304 Calliope Street - Renwick Variance Request; Project No. VR-24-03. (Planner I Belizaire)

attachments.name: Fourth Amendment to JPA_FLU Map Amendment

description:
The area proposed for the Fourth Amendment to the City of Ocoee-Orange County Joint Planning Area (JPA) is comprised of seven (7) parcels, assigned parcel ID numbers 07-22-28-0000-00-074, 07-22-28-0000-00-105, 07-22-28-0000-00-039, 07-22-28-0000-00-041, 07-22-28-0000-00-043, 07-22-28-0000-00-057 and 07-22-28-0000-00-060. These properties are part of the Ocoee Regional Sports Complex Planned Unit Development (PUD). Five (5) of the subject properties (parcels ending in -039, -043, -074, and -105) are located on the east side of Ocoee Apopka Road, and the remaining two (2) are generally located on the west side of North Lakewood Avenue. Combined they consist of approximately 17.87 acres. The applicant proposes to develop the 150-acre Ocoee Regional Sports Complex project, which will include baseball fields, retail, restaurant, hotel, civic/assembly, office, indoor sports, and other commercial uses.
In order for the proposed project to proceed, the JPA Future Land Use Map (FLUM) needs to be amended to change the land use designation of the subject properties from Low Density Residential (LDR) to Commercial (COMM). Though the proposed Commercial FLUM designation within the City permits up to a 3.0 floor area ratio, the proposed Regional Sports Complex includes a Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan Future Land Use Map and Text Amendment, which, among other parameters, limits the maximum FAR to 0.4 and establishes a maximum development program of 1.33 MSF of commercial (inclusive of the square footage of the hotel buildings) and maximum net new external daily traffic trips of 17,960 trips. Evaluation of impacts from the proposed project on transportation, utilities and natural resources was conducted as part of the Large-Scale Comprehensive Plan FLUM and Text Amendment and Rezoning processes.
The proposed Fourth JPA Amendment is consistent with the City's goals of increasing availability of commercial lands and improving economic opportunities in the city limits.

attachments.name: Business Impact Estimate Form - Ordinance Updating Chapter 45, Arbor Code

description:
On November 7, 2023, the Ocoee City Commission placed a moratorium on tree removal permits whereby Homeowners Association (HOA) or Property Owners Association (POA) requests a form of blanket tree removal permit to remove more than one (1) tree in a private right-of-way, landscape buffer, or common open space. Also, based on a new State law passed in 2022, the Florida legislature amended Section 163.045, Florida Statutes, to limit the circumstances under which the owners of residential property can remove trees without a permit and to require, at the time of tree removal, possession of documentation of an onsite Tree Risk Assessment report meeting industry standards signed by a certified arborist or licensed landscape architect.
On March 5, 2024, the Ocoee City Commission directed staff to evaluate and develop standards for tree pruning and maintenance, especially as they relate to street trees and utility lines.
Thus, staff is proposing an amendment to Chapter 45, Arbor Code, within the Code of Ordinances, in order to:Update the definition of "protected tree",
Clarify and revise regulations relative to tree removal requirements, including application, review process, and determination of just cause,
Provide a process for City Commission review of tree removal applications in residential developments when such applications are within private residential right-of-ways, landscape buffers, parking areas, and common open space areas,
Establish regulations relative to tree removal in conformance with Section 163.045, Florida Statutes,
Clarify the purposes of tree pruning and provide regulations on tree pruning and maintenance, and
List prohibited activities and techniques.
Staff anticipates bringing this back to the Commission for second reading at the February 18, 2025, City Commission Meeting.
title: First Reading of Ordinance Updating Chapter 45, Arbor Code, Code of Ordinances, Regarding Tree Removal Process. (Development Services Director Corless)

attachments.name: Bid Proposal - Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater Southeast, LLC

description:
The City of Ocoee solicited sealed bids from accredited/certified laboratories, “Service Providers”, to furnish all necessary labor, supplies, materials, equipment, and incidental items to satisfactorily perform the laboratory services and sampling procedures detailed in these technical specifications on an “as needed basis.” The services include analytical laboratory services to perform testing of surface water, groundwater from Surficial and Floridan aquifer water supply wells, monitoring wells, potable drinking water, raw and treated wastewater, industrial wastewater from facilities discharging to the city’s wastewater collection system, reclaimed water, wastewater residuals and groundwater from groundwater monitoring wells for a reclaimed water system. The proposal also includes sampling, field analyses, and sample pickup services.
All sampling, analyses and reporting shall be done in accordance with the United States Environmental Protection Agency, Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP), Florida Department of Health (FDOH), and TNI standards. The work shall be in compliance with all applicable FDEP SOPs. Bids were advertised on August 2,2026, and publicly opened on September 22, 2026, and three (3) bids were received. Total base bid amounts ranged from $35,672.00 to $78,220.00.
The City originally intended to award a primary and secondary firm. However, in the best interest of the City, the Utilities Department recommends awarding all three (3) laboratories. Three providers offer additional testing options and backup capacity, support completion of analyses within required compliance time frames, and provide flexibility to manage service availability, fuel surcharges, and future price fluctuations.
Per Asst. Director Trent Hopper, the Utilities Department recommends Eurofins as the primary laboratory based on its lowest total base bid, with Advanced Environmental Laboratories and Tri-Tech as secondary laboratories. Utilities intends to assign most of the work to Eurofins and distribute the remaining work between the secondary laboratories based on operational needs, testing capabilities, pricing, availability, and required turnaround times. The proposed contract for the initial period of three (3) years, with two (2) automatic one-year extensions.
Eurofins and Tri-Tech are on the existing contract with the City and Advanced Labs will be an addition to this.

Public Works vehicle #1255 (Ford F-150 4x4 XL) was involved in a rear-end motor vehicle collision on August 31, 2026. City staff determined that the City was not at fault in this incident. The City’s insurance carrier subsequently declared the vehicle a total loss and issued proceeds in the amount of $22,420.00.
The Public Works Department is responsible for maintaining a fully operational fleet and has an immediate need to replace this vehicle. Current industry conditions indicate extended delivery and lead times, up to several months in some cases, for this type of vehicle.
The City's Fleet Division received a quote for the replacement from Duval Ford that exactly matches the specifications of vehicle #1255 at a purchase price of $45,559.00 using the Florida Sheriffs Association Light Vehicle Contract FSA 25VEL-33. In FY27, the Public Works Department (Stormwater) budgeted $45,000 for a Traffic Scorpion Crash Attenuator Trailer (Job A000624), however, this item will be purchased through the General Fund (Streets) fund. The available funds will be reallocated to cover the remaining balance of $23,139.00.
Staff are requesting authorization from the Commission to proceed with the purchase using the insurance proceeds, to reallocate the budgeted funds from the Traffic Scorpion Crash Attenuator Trailer to cover the difference, and to authorize the City Manager to approve a price deviation of up to five percent (5%) to accommodate any potential price fluctuations.

description:
The City of Ocoee Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) utilizes two Smith & Loveless Pista Grit systems to remove grit, sand, and other abrasive sediment from the wastewater stream prior to treatment. These systems play a critical role in protecting downstream equipment by reducing excessive wear and tear on pumps, piping, and other treatment process components.
The approved Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Utilities Department Budget includes $88,000.00 for the scheduled 10-year replacement of the Smith & Loveless Pista Grit No. 2 system. The existing equipment is approaching the end of its useful service life, and timely replacement is necessary to maintain reliable plant operations and protect critical downstream infrastructure from premature deterioration and maintenance costs.
Environmental Equipment Services, LLC is the sole source provider and authorized representative for Smith & Loveless equipment and replacement components.
title: Approval to Replace Pista Grit 2 at the City of Ocoee Wastewater Treatment Plant. (Utilities Director Bolling)

description:
The approved City of Ocoee Budget for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 includes funding for the replacement of a Lift Station By-Pass Pump in accordance with the Utilities Department’s 10-year equipment maintenance and replacement plan. A bypass pump temporarily reroutes wastewater during maintenance, rehabilitation, power outages, or mechanical failures. The bypass pump is essential to maintain uninterrupted wastewater service while preventing sanitary sewer overflows. Funding for this replacement was approved in the FY26/27 budget under Wastewater Field Operations in the amount of $80,000.00.
The replacement bypass pump quote was procured through the Florida Sheriffs Association Cooperative Purchasing Program, which provides competitively solicited contracts for public agencies throughout the State of Florida (FSA 26-EQU24.0, Specification #313). Xylem, formerly Godwin, provided a quote for $72,477.40.
The scheduled replacement of critical utility equipment allows the Utility Department to strategically manage capital expenditures by spreading the cost of high-value equipment replacements over multiple fiscal years. This planned approach helps ensure the continued reliability of utility operations while preventing any single budget year from being disproportionately impacted by large equipment replacement costs.
title: Approval to Purchase Budgeted Bypass Pump Fiscal Year 26/27. (Utilities Director Bolling)
